# Canonical Seed Specification - E-Commerce - Stage 4

## Architectural breaking change: Option A
Migrate the inherited Stage 3 application from a monolithic backend into independently running microservices with real RabbitMQ events. Preserve the working React/TypeScript frontend, Python/FastAPI stack, catalog, cart, authentication, simulated checkout, reviews with images, moderation, caching, automated tests and coverage. This is an architectural migration, not a new set of business features.

## Required migration
- Run at least three independently startable Python/FastAPI business services with explicit ownership boundaries: identity/authentication; commerce (catalog and simulated checkout); reviews (review submission, images and moderation). A thin HTTP gateway may preserve the existing frontend API contract. A gateway must delegate over HTTP, not execute the old monolithic business handlers. More services are optional only if justified.
- Give each service ownership of its state and storage. Separate local SQLite files are sufficient. No shared writable database, cross-service database reads, shared Python singleton state, in-process HTTP transports, or mounting all applications into one process as a substitute for microservices. Shared contract/schema utilities are allowed.
- Use a real RabbitMQ AMQP broker. Integrate it into a business flow: review moderation events update a commerce-owned public review projection and invalidate relevant caches. Pending/rejected reviews remain hidden; approved reviews and their images become public within a documented bounded eventual-consistency window. No in-memory bus or logging-only event demonstration as a substitute for broker integration.
- Document versioned JSON event contracts with event identity, correlation identity, type, timestamp and payload. Use durable queues/messages, publisher confirmation, manual acknowledgements after successful processing, idempotent consumers, bounded retry/dead-letter handling and reconnect backoff. Persist outgoing business events transactionally with domain changes (a small SQLite outbox is sufficient) so a broker outage does not silently lose an accepted moderation change. Do not claim exactly-once delivery.
- Authenticate and authorize internal HTTP operations without trusting client-supplied role headers. Preserve moderator/customer separation, existing demo credentials and frontend-visible behavior. Keep private responses uncached and public projections coherent after events. Keep image visibility consistent with moderation.
- Supply a documented Windows/PowerShell local launch/stop procedure, readiness checks and environment-based service/broker addresses. Read stage4-runtime.json for tool-isolated local ports and AMQP vhost; those are deployment parameters, not different functional requirements. Provide a Compose stack with RabbitMQ, services, gateway and frontend, and update CI, coverage commands and E2E setup for the distributed architecture. No paid cloud services or external deployment.

## Verification and native workflow
First inspect only relevant Stage 3 native specs and implementation, then create all native Stage 4 requirements, architecture/design, API/event contracts and implementation tasks before implementation. Make delegated choices explicitly and concisely. The researcher preauthorizes specs and implementation and accepts reasonable differences between tools; do not ask questions or wait for approvals. All prompts, specs, code, comments, UI and documentation must be in English. Any correction to code must follow a native spec clarification. Preserve earlier-stage and sibling workspaces and do not read or modify external evaluation files.
Verify with meaningful service tests and real multi-process, real-broker integration/E2E tests: purchasing, customer submission, hidden pending review, moderator approval, event-driven public visibility and customer access denial. Prove actual cross-process event propagation; also test duplicate delivery and a broker/consumer outage followed by recovery without losing the accepted change. Test adapters may support focused unit tests but cannot substitute for the real-broker acceptance run. Collect raw backend coverage.xml and frontend lcov.info, run a successful frontend production build, and retain inherited functional checks appropriate to the refactor. Do not invent coverage targets. If Docker is unavailable, validate natively with the provisioned broker and state that container execution is unverified.
Minimize credits: concise specs, targeted file reads, practical tests, no repeated exact-spec audits or unrelated refactors. Stop repeating successful checks unless source changes justify them. Provide exact startup/testing commands and actual limitations in README.md. Finish specs and runnable migrated code.

</content>
</file>

<file name="c:\Users\jeron\OneDrive\Escritorio\uni\implementacion Ecommerce\Caso 3-Ecommerce\Etapa 4\Kiro\README.md" language="markdown" >
<content>
# E-Commerce Stage 1 + Stage 2 + Stage 3

This repository contains a demonstration e-commerce application generated for the SDD tools comparison. It consists of a React and TypeScript frontend and a Python and FastAPI backend.

**Stage 1** delivers the core purchasing journey: browse the catalog, manage a local cart, register or sign in, and complete a simulated checkout.

**Stage 2** adds **product reviews with images and moderation** on top of Stage 1, without changing the Stage 1 journey. A signed-in customer can submit a review (star rating, text, optional title, and up to three images) for a product; every review enters a moderation queue; a moderator approves or rejects it; and only approved reviews are shown publicly on the product together with an aggregate rating summary. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/` (requirements, design, tasks) and the inherited Stage 1 spec in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage1/`.

**Stage 3** adds **architecture and automated delivery verification** (Option A) on top of Stage 2, without changing any application behavior: real end-to-end (Playwright) tests against the running stack, a CI pipeline (install → test with coverage → build → E2E), reproducible multi-stage Docker builds with a one-command local orchestration, and bounded caching for the public catalog read endpoints. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/` (requirements, design, tasks). The quickest way to run and verify Stage 3 is the [Stage 3 section below](#stage-3-e2e-tests-ci-containers-and-caching).

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.11 or later
- Node.js 18 or later
- npm

## Project structure

```text
backend/    FastAPI API, services, data access, and backend tests
frontend/   React application, client-side state, and frontend tests
.kiro/      Kiro specification artifacts
```

## Run the application

The backend and frontend must run in separate terminals.

### 1. Start the backend

Open a terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

On macOS or Linux, activate the virtual environment with:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

The backend will be available at:

- API: <http://localhost:8000>
- Health check: <http://localhost:8000/health>
- Interactive API documentation: <http://localhost:8000/docs>

### 2. Start the frontend

Open a second terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173> in a browser.

The frontend expects the backend to be running at `http://localhost:8000`.

## Run the tests

### Backend

With the backend virtual environment activated:

```powershell
cd backend
pytest
```

### Frontend

```powershell
cd frontend
npm test
```

## Build the frontend

To type-check the frontend and create a production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

The generated production files will be placed in `frontend/dist`.

## Stage 2: reviews, images, and moderation

### How to try it

1. Start the backend and frontend as described above (two terminals). The backend seeds a demonstration moderator account automatically at startup.
2. In the browser, open a product's **View details** panel in the Catalog. The expanded panel shows the product's approved reviews, a rating summary, and — when you are signed in as a customer — a review submission form.
3. **Submit a review** as a customer: register or sign in on the **Account** view, then expand a product, choose a rating, write the review text (optionally a title), optionally attach up to three images, and submit. The review is created as `pending` and is not yet publicly visible.
4. **Moderate** the review: sign out, then sign in with the moderator credentials below and open the **Moderation** destination in the top navigation. The pending review appears in the queue with its product, rating, text, images, and author. Approve it to make it publicly visible (and counted in the rating summary) or reject it to keep it hidden.
5. Re-open the product's details as any visitor: approved reviews and the rating summary are now shown.

### Moderator demonstration credentials

A single built-in moderator account is seeded at backend startup so the moderation workflow can be demonstrated immediately:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

These are a local-demo convenience defined in `backend/app/services/moderator_seed.py`. Sign in with them on the Account view; the **Moderation** view then becomes usable. A regular customer account cannot access moderation.

### Stage 2 endpoints (added additively over the Stage 1 six)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Approved reviews + rating summary for a product |
| `POST` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Submit a review (active customer session required) |
| `GET` | `/reviews/images/{imageId}` | Serve a stored review image |
| `GET` | `/moderation/reviews` | Pending moderation queue (moderator session required) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/approve` | Approve a pending review (moderator) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/reject` | Reject a pending review (moderator) |

## Important implementation notes

- The catalog, account, and review data use an in-process demonstration store; nothing is persisted durably across backend restarts.
- Review **image bytes** are the only on-disk artifact: they are written to the git-ignored folder `backend/app/data/review_images/` and served through the backend. No external object storage, CDN, or paid service is used.
- Review images are submitted as base64-encoded data in the JSON request, validated (type allow-list JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP, max 2 MB, up to 3 per review), and only then stored.
- Moderation states are `pending`, `approved`, and `rejected`; a decision is terminal. A customer may submit at most one review per product, and submitted reviews cannot be edited or deleted. These and other delegated decisions are documented as assumptions A1–A8 in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/requirements.md`.
- The cart and session state are kept in frontend memory and are reset when the page is reloaded.
- Checkout is simulated. No real payment is processed and no order is persisted.
- All interface text, code, comments, and specifications are in English.

## Stage 3: E2E tests, CI, containers, and caching

Stage 3 is additive: the nine existing endpoints' request/response bodies are unchanged except for added cache/freshness response headers, and the frontend journeys and views are unchanged. The native Stage 3 spec lives in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/`.

### Demo / moderator credentials

The seeded moderator account (used by the review-lifecycle E2E test and by manual moderation) is unchanged from Stage 2:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

### Exact startup commands (PowerShell)

Run the backend and frontend in two terminals from the repository root.

Backend (first terminal):

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

Frontend (second terminal):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The frontend calls the backend at `http://localhost:8000`.

### Exact testing / verification commands (PowerShell)

Backend tests with a raw coverage report (`backend/coverage.xml`, Cobertura):

```powershell
cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install coverage
coverage run -m pytest
coverage xml -o coverage.xml
```

Frontend unit/integration tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run test:coverage
```

Frontend production build (type-check + Vite build into `frontend/dist`):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

Real end-to-end tests (Playwright boots the real backend and the production build, then drives Chromium). Run once to install the browser, then run the suite:

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

The E2E suite covers three journeys: the Stage 1 purchasing journey, the Stage 2 review lifecycle (submit → pending/hidden → moderator approval → public), and a moderation access-denied check for a regular customer. The Playwright config starts `uvicorn` from `backend/` (using `backend/.venv` when present) on port 8000 and `vite preview` on port 4173; if a server cannot start, the run fails loudly rather than passing against a dead stack.

### Bounded public API caching

- Only the two session-independent public catalog reads are cached: `GET /products` and `GET /products/{id}`.
- The cache is in-process and bounded by both a per-entry TTL and a maximum entry count. Defaults: TTL `30s` (`CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, set `0` to disable), max entries `256` (`CATALOG_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`).
- Cached responses carry `X-Cache: HIT|MISS` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>`. Session-varying and authenticated responses — `GET /products/{id}/reviews` (it includes the caller's own review), `/auth/*`, and `/moderation/*` — are marked `Cache-Control: no-store` and are **never** shared-cached, so no per-user data can leak between callers.
- **Invalidation / freshness:** the review-listing endpoint is intentionally uncached, so a newly approved review is immediately publicly visible; a moderation approve/reject additionally calls a cache-invalidation hook. Stale catalog entries cannot outlive their TTL.

Example (observe the cache headers):

```powershell
# First call: X-Cache: MISS ; second call within the TTL: X-Cache: HIT
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
```

### Containers and one-command local orchestration

Reproducible multi-stage builds are provided: `backend/Dockerfile` (`python:3.11-slim` builder + slim runtime, uvicorn on container port 8000) and `frontend/Dockerfile` (`node:20-alpine` build stage → `nginx:1.27-alpine` serving the static build on container port 80). A single orchestration command starts both with a user-defined bridge network and a `/health` readiness healthcheck on the backend:

```powershell
docker compose up --build
```

<content>
# E-Commerce Stage 1 + Stage 2 + Stage 3

This repository contains a demonstration e-commerce application generated for the SDD tools comparison. It consists of a React and TypeScript frontend and a Python and FastAPI backend.

**Stage 1** delivers the core purchasing journey: browse the catalog, manage a local cart, register or sign in, and complete a simulated checkout.

**Stage 2** adds **product reviews with images and moderation** on top of Stage 1, without changing the Stage 1 journey. A signed-in customer can submit a review (star rating, text, optional title, and up to three images) for a product; every review enters a moderation queue; a moderator approves or rejects it; and only approved reviews are shown publicly on the product together with an aggregate rating summary. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/` (requirements, design, tasks) and the inherited Stage 1 spec in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage1/`.

**Stage 3** adds **architecture and automated delivery verification** (Option A) on top of Stage 2, without changing any application behavior: real end-to-end (Playwright) tests against the running stack, a CI pipeline (install → test with coverage → build → E2E), reproducible multi-stage Docker builds with a one-command local orchestration, and bounded caching for the public catalog read endpoints. See the native specification in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/` (requirements, design, tasks). The quickest way to run and verify Stage 3 is the [Stage 3 section below](#stage-3-e2e-tests-ci-containers-and-caching).

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.11 or later
- Node.js 18 or later
- npm

## Project structure

```text
backend/    FastAPI API, services, data access, and backend tests
frontend/   React application, client-side state, and frontend tests
.kiro/      Kiro specification artifacts
```

## Run the application

The backend and frontend must run in separate terminals.

### 1. Start the backend

Open a terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

On macOS or Linux, activate the virtual environment with:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

The backend will be available at:

- API: <http://localhost:8000>
- Health check: <http://localhost:8000/health>
- Interactive API documentation: <http://localhost:8000/docs>

### 2. Start the frontend

Open a second terminal in the repository root and run:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173> in a browser.

The frontend expects the backend to be running at `http://localhost:8000`.

## Run the tests

### Backend

With the backend virtual environment activated:

```powershell
cd backend
pytest
```

### Frontend

```powershell
cd frontend
npm test
```

## Build the frontend

To type-check the frontend and create a production build:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

The generated production files will be placed in `frontend/dist`.

## Stage 2: reviews, images, and moderation

### How to try it

1. Start the backend and frontend as described above (two terminals). The backend seeds a demonstration moderator account automatically at startup.
2. In the browser, open a product's **View details** panel in the Catalog. The expanded panel shows the product's approved reviews, a rating summary, and — when you are signed in as a customer — a review submission form.
3. **Submit a review** as a customer: register or sign in on the **Account** view, then expand a product, choose a rating, write the review text (optionally a title), optionally attach up to three images, and submit. The review is created as `pending` and is not yet publicly visible.
4. **Moderate** the review: sign out, then sign in with the moderator credentials below and open the **Moderation** destination in the top navigation. The pending review appears in the queue with its product, rating, text, images, and author. Approve it to make it publicly visible (and counted in the rating summary) or reject it to keep it hidden.
5. Re-open the product's details as any visitor: approved reviews and the rating summary are now shown.

### Moderator demonstration credentials

A single built-in moderator account is seeded at backend startup so the moderation workflow can be demonstrated immediately:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

These are a local-demo convenience defined in `backend/app/services/moderator_seed.py`. Sign in with them on the Account view; the **Moderation** view then becomes usable. A regular customer account cannot access moderation.

### Stage 2 endpoints (added additively over the Stage 1 six)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Approved reviews + rating summary for a product |
| `POST` | `/products/{id}/reviews` | Submit a review (active customer session required) |
| `GET` | `/reviews/images/{imageId}` | Serve a stored review image |
| `GET` | `/moderation/reviews` | Pending moderation queue (moderator session required) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/approve` | Approve a pending review (moderator) |
| `POST` | `/moderation/reviews/{reviewId}/reject` | Reject a pending review (moderator) |

## Important implementation notes

- The catalog, account, and review data use an in-process demonstration store; nothing is persisted durably across backend restarts.
- Review **image bytes** are the only on-disk artifact: they are written to the git-ignored folder `backend/app/data/review_images/` and served through the backend. No external object storage, CDN, or paid service is used.
- Review images are submitted as base64-encoded data in the JSON request, validated (type allow-list JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP, max 2 MB, up to 3 per review), and only then stored.
- Moderation states are `pending`, `approved`, and `rejected`; a decision is terminal. A customer may submit at most one review per product, and submitted reviews cannot be edited or deleted. These and other delegated decisions are documented as assumptions A1–A8 in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/requirements.md`.
- The cart and session state are kept in frontend memory and are reset when the page is reloaded.
- Checkout is simulated. No real payment is processed and no order is persisted.
- All interface text, code, comments, and specifications are in English.

## Stage 3: E2E tests, CI, containers, and caching

Stage 3 is additive: the nine existing endpoints' request/response bodies are unchanged except for added cache/freshness response headers, and the frontend journeys and views are unchanged. The native Stage 3 spec lives in `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/`.

### Demo / moderator credentials

The seeded moderator account (used by the review-lifecycle E2E test and by manual moderation) is unchanged from Stage 2:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | `moderator` |
| Password | `moderator123` |

### Exact startup commands (PowerShell)

Run the backend and frontend in two terminals from the repository root.

Backend (first terminal):

```powershell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

Frontend (second terminal):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The frontend calls the backend at `http://localhost:8000`.

### Exact testing / verification commands (PowerShell)

Backend tests with a raw coverage report (`backend/coverage.xml`, Cobertura):

```powershell
cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install coverage
coverage run -m pytest
coverage xml -o coverage.xml
```

Frontend unit/integration tests with a raw coverage report (`frontend/coverage/lcov.info`, LCOV):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run test:coverage
```

Frontend production build (type-check + Vite build into `frontend/dist`):

```powershell
cd frontend
npm run build
```

Real end-to-end tests (Playwright boots the real backend and the production build, then drives Chromium). Run once to install the browser, then run the suite:

```powershell
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

The E2E suite covers three journeys: the Stage 1 purchasing journey, the Stage 2 review lifecycle (submit → pending/hidden → moderator approval → public), and a moderation access-denied check for a regular customer. The Playwright config starts `uvicorn` from `backend/` (using `backend/.venv` when present) on port 8000 and `vite preview` on port 4173; if a server cannot start, the run fails loudly rather than passing against a dead stack.

### Bounded public API caching

- Only the two session-independent public catalog reads are cached: `GET /products` and `GET /products/{id}`.
- The cache is in-process and bounded by both a per-entry TTL and a maximum entry count. Defaults: TTL `30s` (`CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, set `0` to disable), max entries `256` (`CATALOG_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`).
- Cached responses carry `X-Cache: HIT|MISS` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>`. Session-varying and authenticated responses — `GET /products/{id}/reviews` (it includes the caller's own review), `/auth/*`, and `/moderation/*` — are marked `Cache-Control: no-store` and are **never** shared-cached, so no per-user data can leak between callers.
- **Invalidation / freshness:** the review-listing endpoint is intentionally uncached, so a newly approved review is immediately publicly visible; a moderation approve/reject additionally calls a cache-invalidation hook. Stale catalog entries cannot outlive their TTL.

Example (observe the cache headers):

```powershell
# First call: X-Cache: MISS ; second call within the TTL: X-Cache: HIT
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
(Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8000/products -UseBasicParsing).Headers['X-Cache']
```

### Containers and one-command local orchestration

Reproducible multi-stage builds are provided: `backend/Dockerfile` (`python:3.11-slim` builder + slim runtime, uvicorn on container port 8000) and `frontend/Dockerfile` (`node:20-alpine` build stage → `nginx:1.27-alpine` serving the static build on container port 80). A single orchestration command starts both with a user-defined bridge network and a `/health` readiness healthcheck on the backend:

```powershell
docker compose up --build
```

This publishes the backend on host port 8000 and the frontend on host port 8080 (open <http://localhost:8080>). Because the backend is published on host 8000, the frontend's existing `http://localhost:8000` API base URL keeps working unchanged. No external or paid service is used and nothing is deployed.

> **Runtime note (honest limitation):** Docker was **not available** in the environment where this stage was validated (`docker` is not on PATH). The `Dockerfile`s, `nginx.conf`, and `docker-compose.yml` were validated by inspection and are exercised by the CI definition, but **a local container run was not executed and is not claimed.** Run `docker compose up --build` on a machine with Docker installed to start the containerized stack.

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on push and pull request: it installs backend and frontend dependencies, runs the backend tests producing `coverage.xml`, runs the frontend unit tests producing `lcov.info`, builds the frontend, installs the Playwright browser, runs the E2E suite against the real stack, and uploads the coverage reports and the Playwright report as artifacts. It does **not** publish or deploy to any external infrastructure.

> **Coverage note:** the coverage reports (`backend/coverage.xml`, `frontend/coverage/lcov.info`) are produced for later quality analysis. No coverage target is prescribed and no unexecuted check is claimed as passed.

# Requirements Document

## Introduction

Stage 3 evolves the inherited Stage 2 demonstration e-commerce application along **Stage 3 Option A: architecture and automated delivery verification**. It adds real end-to-end (E2E) tests against the running frontend and backend, a continuous-integration (CI) pipeline that installs, tests, measures coverage, builds, and runs the E2E checks, reproducible multi-stage Docker builds with a simple local orchestration command, and bounded response caching for suitable public read endpoints.

Stage 3 is purely additive to application behavior. The Stage 1 purchasing journey (browse the catalog, manage a local cart, register or sign in, complete a simulated checkout) and the Stage 2 reviews-with-images-and-moderation workflow are preserved unchanged. Stage 3 changes how the application is verified, packaged, and served, not what the application does for an end user.

This document derives its scope from `canonical-seed-stage-3.md`. The seed deliberately leaves several operational details undecided (E2E tool choice, cache TTLs, container base images, orchestration tooling) and delegates those choices to the tool. Each such choice is recorded as a numbered assumption in the **Assumptions** section and treated as a first-class requirement. The researcher preauthorizes these assumptions, the specs, and the implementation; no approval gates apply.

Like earlier stages, the application stays local and easy to demonstrate: no paid external services, no external deployment, and no architecture rewrite. All artifacts, source code, comments, documentation, and user-facing text are in English.

## Relationship to Stages 1 and 2

- Stage 1 (`.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage1/`) and Stage 2 (`.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage2/`) artifacts remain authoritative for application behavior and are not modified by Stage 3. This Stage 3 spec lives at `.kiro/specs/ecommerce-stage3/` and references the earlier stages where it builds on them.
- Stage 3 keeps the existing stack: a React + TypeScript (Vite) frontend and a Python + FastAPI backend that run and are reviewed separately and communicate over HTTP/JSON.
- Stage 3 preserves the nine HTTP endpoints across Stages 1 and 2 (six Stage 1 + three Stage 2 route groups) and the existing in-process demonstration data store plus local on-disk review images. It adds no new application endpoints; caching, containers, CI, and E2E are cross-cutting concerns layered on top.

## Glossary

- **E2E test**: An automated browser-driven test that exercises the real frontend talking to the real backend over HTTP, with no request mocking at the boundary under test.
- **CI pipeline**: An automated workflow that installs dependencies, runs backend and frontend tests with coverage, builds the frontend, and runs the E2E checks, without deploying anywhere.
- **Multi-stage build**: A Docker build that separates a build/dependency stage from a slim runtime stage to produce a smaller, reproducible runtime image.
- **Orchestration command**: A single documented command that starts the frontend and backend containers together with correct networking.
- **Public read endpoint**: A `GET` endpoint whose response does not depend on the caller's session or identity. In this application these are the catalog endpoints `GET /products` and `GET /products/{id}`.
- **Bounded cache**: An in-process response cache with a fixed maximum entry count and a fixed time-to-live (TTL) per entry, so memory and staleness are both bounded.
- **Coverage artifact**: A machine-readable coverage report — backend `coverage.xml` (Cobertura) and frontend `lcov.info` (LCOV) — produced by documented commands for later quality analysis.

## Assumptions

The seed delegates the following decisions to the tool. Each is a deliberate, documented, simple local-demo choice and is binding for Stage 3.

- **A1 — E2E tool.** Playwright is used for E2E tests, driven from the frontend workspace (`frontend/`), because it bundles browser management and a test runner with low setup cost and integrates cleanly with a Vite app. The E2E suite starts the real backend (`uvicorn`) and the real frontend (Vite preview of the production build) and drives a real browser against them. No API calls are mocked inside the browser for the journeys under test.
- **A2 — E2E coverage of journeys.** The E2E suite covers (a) the Stage 1 purchasing journey through simulated checkout, (b) the Stage 2 review lifecycle — submit as a customer, review is hidden while pending, a moderator approves it, and it becomes publicly visible — and (c) an access-denied check: a regular customer cannot reach the moderation queue/actions.
- **A3 — Backend cache scope and policy.** Only the two catalog read endpoints (`GET /products`, `GET /products/{id}`) are cached. They carry no session-specific data, so a shared cache cannot leak between users. `GET /products/{id}/reviews` is **never** shared-cached because its body varies with the caller's session (it includes the caller's own non-approved review); moderation queue responses and any authenticated response are likewise never cached. The cache is in-process, bounded by a maximum entry count, and each entry expires after a short TTL.
- **A4 — Cache TTL and invalidation.** The catalog cache TTL default is 30 seconds (overridable by the `CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` environment variable; `0` disables caching). The catalog is static demonstration data, so TTL expiry is the primary freshness mechanism. Because the seed requires that newly approved reviews become publicly visible correctly, the review-listing endpoint is left uncached; an explicit cache-invalidation hook is additionally invoked on any moderation state change so that, even if review caching were introduced later, approval would immediately invalidate affected entries. No stale catalog entry can outlive its TTL.
- **A5 — Cache correctness headers.** Cached public responses carry an `X-Cache: HIT|MISS` response header for observability and a short `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>` header. Non-cacheable endpoints send `Cache-Control: no-store` so intermediaries do not cache per-user data.
- **A6 — Container images and ports.** The backend image is based on `python:3.11-slim` and runs `uvicorn` on container port 8000. The frontend is built to static files in a build stage and served by `nginx:1.27-alpine` on container port 80, published to host port 8080. A reverse-proxy rule in nginx forwards `/api/*`-style calls is **not** introduced to avoid changing the frontend's existing absolute `http://localhost:8000` base URL; instead the backend is published on host port 8000 so the existing client base URL keeps working unchanged in the local Docker run.
- **A7 — Orchestration tooling.** Docker Compose (`docker-compose.yml`) provides the single orchestration command (`docker compose up --build`). Services share a user-defined bridge network; the backend exposes a `/health` readiness endpoint (already present) used as the Compose healthcheck.
- **A8 — CI platform.** GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the pipeline on push and pull request. It installs backend and frontend dependencies, runs backend tests with `coverage.xml`, runs frontend unit tests with `lcov.info`, builds the frontend, installs Playwright browsers, and runs the E2E suite. It uploads coverage and Playwright artifacts but does not deploy. The CI definition is authoritative documentation of the commands even where a runtime (e.g. Docker) is unavailable locally.
- **A9 — No behavior change.** Stage 3 does not change any request/response body of the nine existing endpoints beyond adding caching/freshness response headers. The frontend's API base URL, views, and journeys are unchanged.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 — End-to-end purchasing journey test

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want an automated E2E test of the purchasing journey, so that catalog → cart → authentication → simulated checkout is verified against the real running stack.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the E2E suite runs the purchasing-journey test THEN it SHALL start the real backend and the real frontend production build and drive a real browser against them without mocking the API boundary.
2. WHEN a user browses the catalog, adds a product to the cart, registers or signs in, and confirms checkout THEN the test SHALL assert a visible checkout confirmation and a reset-to-new-purchase state.
3. IF the backend or frontend is not reachable THEN the test SHALL fail with a clear error rather than passing silently.

### Requirement 2 — End-to-end review lifecycle test

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want an automated E2E test of the review-and-moderation lifecycle, so that the Stage 2 workflow is verified against the real running stack.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a signed-in customer submits a review for a product THEN the test SHALL assert the submission is accepted and the review is NOT publicly visible while pending.
2. WHEN a moderator signs in and approves the pending review THEN the test SHALL assert the review becomes publicly visible with the rating summary updated.
3. WHEN a regular customer attempts to access the moderation queue or a moderation action THEN the test SHALL assert access is denied and no moderation state changes.

### Requirement 3 — CI pipeline

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want a CI pipeline, so that every change is installed, tested, measured, built, and E2E-checked automatically without deploying.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN CI runs THEN it SHALL install backend and frontend dependencies.
2. WHEN CI runs the backend tests THEN it SHALL produce a backend `coverage.xml` artifact.
3. WHEN CI runs the frontend unit tests THEN it SHALL produce a frontend `lcov.info` artifact.
4. WHEN CI builds the frontend THEN the production build SHALL succeed.
5. WHEN CI runs the E2E suite THEN it SHALL start the real stack and execute the Playwright tests.
6. CI SHALL NOT publish or deploy to any external infrastructure.

### Requirement 4 — Reproducible multi-stage containers and orchestration

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want multi-stage Docker builds and a one-command local orchestration, so that the stack runs reproducibly without a bespoke setup.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The backend SHALL have a multi-stage `Dockerfile` producing a slim runtime image that runs the FastAPI app.
2. The frontend SHALL have a multi-stage `Dockerfile` that builds the static assets and serves them from a slim web server image.
3. A single documented orchestration command SHALL start both services with correct container networking.
4. The orchestration SHALL use a documented health/readiness strategy for the backend.
5. The containers SHALL NOT depend on any paid external service or perform any deployment.

### Requirement 5 — Bounded public API caching

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want bounded caching on suitable public read endpoints, so that repeated catalog reads are cheaper without serving stale or cross-user data.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The backend SHALL cache only public read endpoints whose response is independent of the caller's session (`GET /products`, `GET /products/{id}`).
2. The cache SHALL be bounded by a maximum entry count and a per-entry TTL, both documented.
3. A cached response SHALL expire after its TTL so it cannot be served indefinitely.
4. Session-specific or moderation responses SHALL NOT be served from the shared cache and SHALL be marked non-cacheable.
5. WHEN a review is approved THEN the public visibility of that review SHALL be correct on the next read (the review-listing endpoint is uncached, and a cache-invalidation hook fires on moderation state changes).

### Requirement 6 — Coverage artifacts

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want documented commands that produce standard coverage artifacts, so that quality can be analyzed later.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented backend command SHALL produce `coverage.xml` (Cobertura).
2. A documented frontend command SHALL produce `lcov.info` (LCOV).
3. The documentation SHALL NOT invent a coverage target nor claim an unexecuted check passed.

### Requirement 7 — Preservation of earlier stages

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want Stages 1 and 2 preserved, so that Stage 3 adds verification/packaging without regressing behavior.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine existing endpoints' request/response bodies SHALL remain unchanged except for added cache/freshness response headers.
2. The existing frontend journeys and views SHALL remain unchanged.
3. The existing backend and frontend unit/integration test suites SHALL continue to pass.

</content>
</file>

# Design Document — E-Commerce Stage 3 (Architecture & Automated Delivery Verification)

## Overview

Stage 3 layers four cross-cutting concerns onto the unchanged Stage 1 + Stage 2 application: real end-to-end tests, a CI pipeline, reproducible multi-stage containers with one-command orchestration, and bounded caching for public catalog reads. No application endpoint behavior changes beyond the addition of cache/freshness response headers. The stack stays React + TypeScript (Vite) on the frontend and Python + FastAPI on the backend, communicating over HTTP/JSON, with an in-process demonstration data store and local on-disk review images.

The design goals are: (1) verify the real running stack, not mocks; (2) keep caching provably safe against cross-user leakage and review-visibility staleness; (3) make packaging reproducible and runnable with a single command; (4) keep everything local and free of paid services and deployments.

## Architecture

```
            ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │                 CI (GitHub Actions)          │
            │  install → unit tests + coverage → build →   │
            │           Playwright E2E (real stack)        │
            └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │ orchestrates the same commands a developer runs
        ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
        ▼                                         ▼
┌───────────────┐   HTTP/JSON (8000)   ┌───────────────────────┐
│  Frontend     │ ───────────────────▶ │  Backend (FastAPI)    │
│  Vite build   │                      │                       │
│  served by    │                      │  CacheMiddleware ──┐  │
│  nginx:80     │                      │   (public GETs)    │  │
│  (host 8080)  │                      │                    ▼  │
└───────────────┘                      │  routers: catalog, auth,
                                        │  checkout, reviews, moderation
                                        │  in-process stores + on-disk images
                                        └───────────────────────┘
        ▲                                         ▲
        └────────── docker compose up --build ────┘
```

### Caching layer (backend)

A small, self-contained caching module is added and wired as FastAPI middleware. It is the only new backend code and is deliberately minimal.

- `app/services/response_cache.py` — a `BoundedTTLCache`: an in-process dict with insertion-ordered eviction (max N entries) and per-entry TTL. Operations: `get(key)`, `set(key, value)`, `invalidate(predicate=None)`, `clear()`. Entries store the serialized response body, media type, and an expiry timestamp. Thread-unsafe simplicity is acceptable for a single-process demo; a `threading.Lock` guards the dict to be safe under Uvicorn's default worker.
- `app/api/cache_middleware.py` — `CatalogCacheMiddleware` (Starlette `BaseHTTPMiddleware`). On a request it:
  1. Caches **only** `GET /products` and `GET /products/{id}` (exact path match via a compiled allow-list). Everything else passes through untouched and receives `Cache-Control: no-store` if it is an authenticated or session-varying route group (`/moderation`, `/auth`, and `/products/{id}/reviews`), otherwise no cache header is added.
  2. For a cacheable request, builds a key from method + path (no query string is used by these endpoints; no auth/session participates, so the key is user-independent).

"""FastAPI application entry point for the Stage 1 e-commerce backend.

This module wires the API layer into a runnable FastAPI application. Feature
routers (catalog, authentication, checkout) are added in later tasks; this
scaffold exposes a health endpoint so the service is independently runnable
and reviewable (Requirements 14.2, 14.5).

Run locally with:

    uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
"""

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

# Stage 3: bounded response caching for public catalog reads (additive).
from app.api.cache_middleware import CatalogCacheMiddleware

from app.api import auth_register

from app.api import checkout

from app.api import auth_signin

from app.api import catalog

# Stage 2 routers (reviews with images and moderation). Added additively.
from app.api import reviews

from app.api import moderation

from app.services.moderator_seed import seed_moderator

# Default origin for the separately-run frontend development server. The two
# parts communicate exclusively over HTTP/JSON (Requirements 14.3, 14.4).
# Stage 3 additively allows the Vite *preview* origin (port 4173) used by the
# production build and the Playwright E2E suite, and the Docker-published
# frontend origin (host port 8080). These are local-demo origins only.
FRONTEND_DEV_ORIGINS = [
    "http://localhost:5173",
    "http://127.0.0.1:5173",
    "http://localhost:4173",
    "http://127.0.0.1:4173",
    "http://localhost:8080",
    "http://127.0.0.1:8080",
]

app = FastAPI(
    title="E-Commerce Stage 1 Backend",
    version="0.1.0",
    description=(
        "Demonstration backend for the Stage 1 e-commerce journey. Serves "
        "catalog data, account data, authentication, and a non-persistent "
        "checkout confirmation over HTTP/JSON."
    ),
)

# Stage 3: bounded, TTL-based caching for the two session-independent public
# catalog reads (GET /products, GET /products/{id}); session-varying and
# moderation responses are marked no-store. Added additively; it does not
# change any endpoint's request/response body (Requirements 5.1, 5.4, 7.1).
#
# Ordering matters: FastAPI/Starlette applies the LAST-added middleware as the
# OUTERMOST layer. The cache is added FIRST (so it is the inner layer) and CORS
# is added AFTER it (so CORS is the outer layer). This guarantees CORS headers
# are applied to every response — including cached HITs that this middleware
# constructs itself — so the browser is never blocked on a cached catalog read.
app.add_middleware(CatalogCacheMiddleware)

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=FRONTEND_DEV_ORIGINS,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)


@app.get("/health", tags=["system"])
def health() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Report that the service is running. Used by smoke/structural checks."""
    return {"status": "ok"}


# Registration endpoint (POST /auth/register). Added additively; other auth
# routes (sign-in/sign-out) are registered by their own task.
app.include_router(auth_register.router)

# Sign-in/sign-out endpoints (POST /auth/login, POST /auth/logout).
app.include_router(auth_signin.router)

# Non-persistent simulated-purchase confirmation (POST /checkout/confirm,
# Requirements 10.1, 10.2). Added additively by task 5.1.
app.include_router(checkout.router)


# Feature routers are registered here as later tasks implement them.
app.include_router(catalog.router)

# Stage 2: reviews (submission, public reviews, image serving) and moderation
# (moderator-only queue + approve/reject). Added additively; the six Stage 1
# endpoints are unchanged (Requirement 9.5).
app.include_router(reviews.router)
app.include_router(moderation.router)


@app.on_event("startup")
def _seed_demo_moderator() -> None:
    """Seed the demonstration moderator account at startup (Assumption A5).

    Idempotent: safe to run on every startup. The moderator credentials are
    documented in the project README so the moderation workflow can be
    demonstrated immediately.
    """
    seed_moderator()

</content>

from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

<content>
"""Registration endpoint (API layer).

Exposes ``POST /auth/register`` for the credential contract (``identifier`` +
``password``). It validates request shape, delegates to the registration
service, and returns JSON responses with appropriate status codes.

On success it returns the created account's public identity only — never the
password and never the stored ``passwordHash`` (Requirements 7.2, 7.3). On
failure it returns a structured JSON error that names each empty required item
and each non-conforming item (Requirements 5.3, 5.4) and that never echoes any
submitted credential value (Requirements 5.5, 7.4).

This router lives in its own module so the authentication feature can be built
incrementally without colliding with the sign-in/sign-out work. It is included
additively by ``app.main``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fastapi import APIRouter, status
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel

from app.services.registration_service import (
    IdentifierTakenError,
    RegistrationError,
    register,
)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["authentication"])


class RegisterRequest(BaseModel):
    """Registration request body for the credential contract.

    The ``password`` is accepted only as input here; it is never stored or
    returned as readable plain text (Requirements 7.2, 7.3). Fields are typed
    as optional text so that missing or empty items reach the service layer,
    which is the single place that classifies offending items (R5.3, R5.4).
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        alias_generator=to_camel,
        populate_by_name=True,
    )

    identifier: str | None = None
    password: str | None = None


class RegisterResponse(BaseModel):
    """Successful registration response.

    Carries only the created account's public identity. It intentionally omits
    the password and the stored ``passwordHash`` so no credential value is ever
    returned (Requirements 7.2, 7.3).
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        alias_generator=to_camel,
        populate_by_name=True,
    )

    id: str
    identifier: str


@router.post(
    "/register",
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    response_model=RegisterResponse,
)
def register_account(request: RegisterRequest) -> RegisterResponse:
    """Create a ``Customer`` account from valid registration input.

    Returns 201 with the new account's public identity on success. Returns 422
    with a structured error naming the offending items on validation failure,
    or 409 when the identifier is already taken. No response ever contains a
    submitted credential value or a stored hash.
    """
    try:
        customer = register(request.identifier, request.password)
    except RegistrationError as error:
        # Structured validation error: name the offending items only, never
        # the submitted credential values (R5.3, R5.4, R5.5).
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
            content={
                "error": "validation_error",
                "message": error.message,
                "emptyFields": error.empty_fields,
                "nonConformingFields": error.non_conforming_fields,
            },
        )
    except IdentifierTakenError as error:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
            content={
                "error": "identifier_taken",
                "message": error.message,
            },
        )

    return RegisterResponse(id=customer.id, identifier=customer.identifier)

"""Authentication sign-in/sign-out API router.

Exposes ``POST /auth/login`` and ``POST /auth/logout`` over HTTP/JSON. The
router validates request shape, delegates to the sign-in service, and maps
outcomes to JSON responses with appropriate status codes. It contains no
business logic and never reaches the data store directly.

- ``POST /auth/login`` accepts ``identifier`` and ``password``; on complete,
  valid input it establishes an active ``Session`` and returns the session
  representation (Requirements 6.1, 6.9). On incomplete/invalid input it
  returns ``401 Unauthorized`` with a uniform authentication error that
  indicates failure without exposing internal detail, hashes, or submitted
  credential values (Requirements 6.3, 7.4). The ``password`` is never
  returned (Requirements 7.2, 7.3).
- ``POST /auth/logout`` ends the active ``Session`` (Requirement 6.6).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fastapi import APIRouter, status
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel

from app.models.session import Session
from app.services.signin_service import AuthenticationError, sign_in, sign_out

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["authentication"])


class LoginRequest(BaseModel):
    """Sign-in request body carrying the credential contract.

    Both fields are typed as optional strings so that missing/empty values are
    handled by the service's uniform authentication failure rather than by a
    separate schema-validation error that could reveal field-level internals.
    The ``password`` is accepted only as input and is never echoed back.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        alias_generator=to_camel,
        populate_by_name=True,
    )

    identifier: str | None = None
    password: str | None = None


def _session_body(session: Session) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Serialize a session for the HTTP response.

    The Stage 1 response shape is ``{active, customerId}``; the Stage 2
    moderator flag (Assumption A5) is added additively and only when it is
    ``True``, so a regular customer's login/logout response keeps the exact
    Stage 1 shape and inherited behavior is preserved (Requirement 9.5). The
    frontend reads ``isModerator`` from a moderator login to gate the
    moderation view.
    """
    body: dict[str, object] = {
        "active": session.active,
        "customerId": session.customer_id,
    }
    if session.is_moderator:
        body["isModerator"] = True
    return body


@router.post("/login")
def login(request: LoginRequest) -> JSONResponse:
    """Validate sign-in input and establish an active Session.

    Returns the active session body (``active`` + ``customerId``, plus
    ``isModerator`` only for a moderator) on success. On incomplete/invalid
    input returns ``401`` with a uniform error message.
    """
    try:
        session = sign_in(request.identifier or "", request.password or "")
    except AuthenticationError as error:
        # Uniform authentication failure; no internal detail, hash, or
        # submitted credential value is included (Requirements 6.3, 7.4).
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            content={"error": str(error)},
        )
    return JSONResponse(status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK, content=_session_body(session))


@router.post("/logout")
def logout() -> JSONResponse:
    """End the active Session, returning the resulting inactive session."""
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK, content=_session_body(sign_out())
    )

<content>
"""Reviews API router (API layer, Stage 2).

Exposes the public and authoring review endpoints over HTTP/JSON:

- ``POST /products/{product_id}/reviews`` - submit a review. Requires an active
  non-moderator customer session (Requirements 1.1, 1.2). Validates the
  submission and creates a ``pending`` review (Requirements 1.3-1.8).
- ``GET /products/{product_id}/reviews`` - list the approved reviews and the
  rating summary for a product, plus the requester's own non-approved review
  when applicable (Requirements 4.1-4.6).
- ``GET /reviews/images/{image_id}`` - stream a stored review image's bytes
  (Requirements 2.6, 2.7).

The router validates request shape and session/authorization, delegates all
business rules to the review service, and maps outcomes to structured JSON
with appropriate status codes. It never exposes internal detail or credential
values (Requirement 6.1).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response

from app.data.accounts import account_store
from app.data.review_images import image_store
from app.data.reviews import review_store
from app.models.review import (
    ProductReviewsResponse,
    RatingSummary,
    Review,
    ReviewResponse,
    ReviewSubmission,
)
from app.services import review_service
from app.services.review_service import (
    DuplicateReviewError,
    ProductNotFoundError,
    ReviewValidationError,
)
from app.services.signin_service import get_current_session

router = APIRouter(tags=["reviews"])


def _resolve_customer_identity() -> str | None:
    """Return the active non-moderator customer's identifier, or ``None``.

    Resolves the module-level session's ``customer_id`` to the account's
    non-sensitive identifier used as a review's author identity. Returns
    ``None`` when there is no active session, when the account cannot be
    resolved, or when the active session is a moderator (a moderator is not a
    review-authoring customer in this demo).
    """
    session = get_current_session()
    if not session.active or session.customer_id is None or session.is_moderator:
        return None
    account = account_store.get_by_id(session.customer_id)
    return account.identifier if account is not None else None


def _to_response(review: Review) -> ReviewResponse:
    """Map a stored ``Review`` onto its safe HTTP/JSON response shape."""
    return ReviewResponse(
        id=review.id,
        product_id=review.product_id,
        author_identity=review.author_identity,
        rating=review.rating,
        title=review.title,
        text=review.text,
        images=[
            {
                "id": image.id,
                "imageUrl": f"/reviews/images/{image.id}",
                "mediaType": image.media_type,
            }
            for image in review.images
        ],
        moderation_state=review.moderation_state,
    )


@router.post(
    "/products/{product_id}/reviews",
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    response_model=ReviewResponse,
)
def submit_review(product_id: str, submission: ReviewSubmission):
    """Submit a review for a product (requires an active customer session)."""
    author_identity = _resolve_customer_identity()
    if author_identity is None:
        # Identification is required to submit a review (R1.2, R6.1).
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            content={
                "error": "authentication_required",
                "message": "You must be signed in as a customer to submit a review.",
            },
        )

    try:
        review = review_service.submit_review(
            product_id=product_id,
            author_identity=author_identity,
            rating=submission.rating,
            text=submission.text,
            title=submission.title,
            images=submission.images,
        )
    except ProductNotFoundError as error:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            content={"error": "product_not_found", "message": error.message},
        )
    except ReviewValidationError as error:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
            content={
                "error": "validation_error",
                "message": error.message,
                "offendingFields": error.offending_fields,
            },
        )
    except DuplicateReviewError as error:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
            content={"error": "duplicate_review", "message": error.message},
        )

    return _to_response(review)


@router.get(
    "/products/{product_id}/reviews",
    response_model=ProductReviewsResponse,
)
def list_product_reviews(product_id: str) -> ProductReviewsResponse:
    """Return approved reviews, the rating summary, and the requester's own review."""
    approved = review_service.list_approved_reviews(product_id)
    summary: RatingSummary = review_service.rating_summary(product_id)

    own: ReviewResponse | None = None
    author_identity = _resolve_customer_identity()
    if author_identity is not None:
        own_review = review_service.own_review(product_id, author_identity)
        if own_review is not None:
            own = _to_response(own_review)

    return ProductReviewsResponse(
        reviews=[_to_response(review) for review in approved],
        summary=summary,
        own_review=own,
    )


@router.get("/reviews/images/{image_id}")
def get_review_image(image_id: str) -> Response:
    """Stream a stored review image's bytes with its media type (R2.6, R2.7)."""
    # Resolve the image's stored filename from the review that references it.
    filename: str | None = None
    for review in review_store.list_all():
        for image in review.images:
            if image.id == image_id:
                filename = image.filename
                break
        if filename is not None:
            break

    if filename is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            detail={
                "error": "image_not_found",
                "message": "No review image exists with that id.",
            },
        )

    try:
        data, media_type = image_store.read(image_id, filename)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND,
            detail={
                "error": "image_not_found",
                "message": "No review image exists with that id.",
            },
        )

    return Response(content=data, media_type=media_type)

</content>

"""Moderation API router (API layer, Stage 2).

Exposes the moderator-only review moderation endpoints over HTTP/JSON:

- ``GET /moderation/reviews`` - list the Moderation_Queue of pending reviews
  (Requirements 3.1, 3.2).
- ``POST /moderation/reviews/{review_id}/approve`` - approve a pending review
  (Requirements 3.3, 3.5, 3.7).
- ``POST /moderation/reviews/{review_id}/reject`` - reject a pending review
  (Requirements 3.4, 3.5, 3.7).

Every endpoint is guarded by an active moderator session: without one, the
request is denied and no state changes (Requirements 3.6, 6.4). The router
delegates all transitions to the review service and maps outcomes to
structured JSON. It never exposes internal detail (Requirement 6.1).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fastapi import APIRouter, status
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from app.models.review import Review, ReviewResponse
from app.services import review_service
from app.services.review_service import ModerationError
from app.services.signin_service import get_current_session

router = APIRouter(prefix="/moderation", tags=["moderation"])


def _moderator_denied_response() -> JSONResponse:
    """Build the uniform denial for a request lacking a moderator session."""
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
        content={
            "error": "moderator_required",
            "message": "Moderator access is required to perform this action.",
        },
    )


def _is_active_moderator() -> bool:
    """Return whether the current session is an active moderator session (A5)."""
    session = get_current_session()
    return session.active and session.is_moderator


def _to_response(review: Review) -> ReviewResponse:
    """Map a stored ``Review`` onto its HTTP/JSON response shape."""
    return ReviewResponse(
        id=review.id,
        product_id=review.product_id,
        author_identity=review.author_identity,
        rating=review.rating,
        title=review.title,
        text=review.text,
        images=[
            {
                "id": image.id,
                "imageUrl": f"/reviews/images/{image.id}",
                "mediaType": image.media_type,
            }
            for image in review.images
        ],
        moderation_state=review.moderation_state,
    )


@router.get("/reviews", response_model=list[ReviewResponse])
def list_moderation_queue():
    """Return the pending moderation queue (moderator session required)."""
    if not _is_active_moderator():
        return _moderator_denied_response()
    pending = review_service.list_pending_reviews()
    return [_to_response(review) for review in pending]


@router.post("/reviews/{review_id}/approve", response_model=ReviewResponse)
def approve_review(review_id: str):
    """Approve a pending review (moderator session required)."""
    if not _is_active_moderator():
        return _moderator_denied_response()
    try:
        review = review_service.approve_review(review_id)
    except ModerationError as error:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
            content={"error": error.code, "message": error.message},
        )
    return _to_response(review)


@router.post("/reviews/{review_id}/reject", response_model=ReviewResponse)
def reject_review(review_id: str):
    """Reject a pending review (moderator session required)."""
    if not _is_active_moderator():
        return _moderator_denied_response()
    try:
        review = review_service.reject_review(review_id)
    except ModerationError as error:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
            content={"error": error.code, "message": error.message},
        )
    return _to_response(review)

"""Catalog response-cache middleware (API layer, Stage 3).

This Starlette middleware adds bounded, TTL-based caching to the two
*session-independent* public catalog reads and marks session-varying or
moderation responses as non-cacheable. It is additive: request and response
bodies of every existing endpoint are unchanged; only cache/freshness response
headers are added (Stage 3 Requirements 5.1, 5.4, 7.1; Assumptions A3, A5).

Cached endpoints (safe to share across all callers):

- ``GET /products``
- ``GET /products/{id}`` (any single-segment product id)

Never cached and explicitly marked ``no-store`` (would vary per user or carry
authenticated data):

- ``/products/{id}/reviews`` — body includes the caller's own non-approved
  review, so it is session-dependent.
- ``/auth/*`` — authentication responses.
- ``/moderation/*`` — moderator-only queue and decisions.

Only ``200`` responses are stored, so errors are never cached. On a hit the
stored body is replayed with ``X-Cache: HIT``; on a miss the downstream body is
returned and stored with ``X-Cache: MISS``. Both carry
``Cache-Control: public, max-age=<ttl>``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.responses import Response

from app.services.response_cache import response_cache

# Exact catalog list, and a single product by id (one path segment, so the
# ``/reviews`` sub-resource is NOT matched).
_PRODUCTS_LIST = re.compile(r"^/products/?$")
_PRODUCT_DETAIL = re.compile(r"^/products/[^/]+/?$")

# Route groups whose responses must never be cached by us or an intermediary.
_NO_STORE_PREFIXES = ("/auth", "/moderation")


def _is_cacheable_path(path: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``path`` is one of the two cacheable catalog reads."""
    return bool(_PRODUCTS_LIST.match(path) or _PRODUCT_DETAIL.match(path))


def _is_sensitive_path(path: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``path`` is session-varying or authenticated.

    These must be marked ``no-store`` so no shared cache (ours or an
    intermediary's) can leak per-user data between callers (Requirement 5.4).
    """
    if path.startswith(_NO_STORE_PREFIXES):
        return True
    # /products/{id}/reviews depends on the caller's session (ownReview).
    return bool(re.match(r"^/products/[^/]+/reviews/?$", path))


class CatalogCacheMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    """Cache the public catalog GETs; mark sensitive responses non-cacheable."""

    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):  # type: ignore[override]
        path = request.url.path
        method = request.method

        cacheable = method == "GET" and _is_cacheable_path(path)

        # Serve a live cache hit without touching downstream.
        if cacheable and response_cache.enabled:
            key = f"GET {path}"
            entry = response_cache.get(key)
            if entry is not None:
                hit = Response(content=entry.body, media_type=entry.media_type)
                hit.headers["X-Cache"] = "HIT"
                hit.headers["Cache-Control"] = (
                    f"public, max-age={response_cache.ttl_seconds}"
                )
                return hit

        response = await call_next(request)

        # Mark session-varying / authenticated responses non-cacheable.
        if _is_sensitive_path(path):
            response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
            return response

        if not cacheable:
            return response

        if not response_cache.enabled:
            # Caching disabled (TTL=0): still advertise freshness semantics.
            response.headers["X-Cache"] = "MISS"
            return response

        # Store only successful responses, so errors are never cached.
        if response.status_code == 200:
            body = b""
            async for chunk in response.body_iterator:  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                body += chunk if isinstance(chunk, bytes) else chunk.encode()
            media_type = response.media_type or "application/json"
            response_cache.set(f"GET {path}", body, media_type)

            fresh = Response(
                content=body,
                status_code=response.status_code,
                media_type=media_type,
            )
            # Preserve any non-cache headers the downstream set.
            for header, value in response.headers.items():
                if header.lower() not in {"content-length", "x-cache", "cache-control"}:
                    fresh.headers[header] = value
            fresh.headers["X-Cache"] = "MISS"
            fresh.headers["Cache-Control"] = (
                f"public, max-age={response_cache.ttl_seconds}"
            )
            return fresh

        response.headers["X-Cache"] = "MISS"
        return response
