<content>
"""Review and moderation service (business logic, Stage 2).

This service owns the Stage 2 business rules:

- Submission validation and review creation (Requirements 1.3-1.8, 2.1-2.5;
  Assumptions A1, A2, A3): rating range, text/title length, image count/type/
  size, one-review-per-author-per-product, and creation in ``pending`` state
  with the author identity recorded.
- Moderation transitions (Requirements 3.1, 3.3-3.5, 3.7; Assumption A4): the
  pending queue, and terminal approve/reject from ``pending``.
- Public visibility and aggregation (Requirements 4.1-4.5; Assumption A8): the
  approved reviews for a product and a rating summary derived from approved
  ratings only.

The service never handles credential values and builds only safe,
client-facing error messages (Requirement 6.1). Image validation and storage
are delegated to the local on-disk image store; a rejected attachment is never
stored (Requirements 2.3, 2.4, 6.3).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

from app.data import catalog
from app.data.review_images import ImageStore, ImageValidationError, image_store
from app.data.reviews import ReviewStore, review_store
from app.models.review import (
    RatingSummary,
    Review,
    ReviewImage,
    ReviewImageInput,
)

# Field bounds (Assumption A2, A3). These are demonstration conveniences.
MIN_RATING = 1
MAX_RATING = 5
MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 2000
MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 120
MAX_IMAGES = 3


class ReviewValidationError(Exception):
    """A review submission failed field validation.

    Carries the exact set of offending field names so the API layer can build
    a structured error. It never carries any submitted credential value
    (Requirement 6.1). ``offending_fields`` is the authoritative set used by
    Property 1; ``message`` is a safe human-readable summary.
    """

    def __init__(self, offending_fields: list[str], message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        # Preserve order but keep it a plain list of unique field names.
        seen: dict[str, None] = {}
        for name in offending_fields:
            seen.setdefault(name, None)
        self.offending_fields = list(seen.keys())
        self.message = message


class DuplicateReviewError(Exception):
    """The author already has a review for this product (Assumption A1)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.message = "You have already reviewed this product. Only one review per product is allowed."
        super().__init__(self.message)


class ProductNotFoundError(Exception):
    """The product being reviewed does not exist in the catalog."""

    def __init__(self, product_id: str) -> None:
        self.product_id = product_id
        self.message = "The product being reviewed does not exist."
        super().__init__(self.message)


class ModerationError(Exception):
    """A moderation action could not be performed.

    Raised for an unknown review or for an attempt to decide a review that is
    not ``pending`` (a decision is terminal, Assumption A4).
    """

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.message = message


def _validate_submission_fields(
    rating: object,
    text: object,
    title: object,
    images: list[ReviewImageInput],
) -> list[str]:
    """Return the set of offending field names for a submission.

    Classifies rating, text, title, and the image set against their rules. The
    returned list is exactly the fields that violate a rule (Property 1).
    Image validation here covers only the count and each image's declared type
    and decoded size, without storing anything.
    """
    offending: list[str] = []

    # Rating: required integer in [MIN_RATING, MAX_RATING] (R1.3).
    if not isinstance(rating, int) or isinstance(rating, bool):
        offending.append("rating")
    elif rating < MIN_RATING or rating > MAX_RATING:
        offending.append("rating")

    # Text: required, non-empty after trimming, <= MAX_TEXT_LENGTH (R1.4, R1.5).
    if not isinstance(text, str) or text.strip() == "":
        offending.append("text")
    elif len(text) > MAX_TEXT_LENGTH:
        offending.append("text")

    # Title: optional; when present must be <= MAX_TITLE_LENGTH (R1.5).
    if title is not None:
        if not isinstance(title, str) or len(title) > MAX_TITLE_LENGTH:
            offending.append("title")

    # Images: count <= MAX_IMAGES (R2.2), then each image's type/size (R2.3,
    # R2.4). The whole image set is reported under the single "images" field.
    if len(images) > MAX_IMAGES:
        offending.append("images")
    else:
        for image in images:
            try:
                image_store.validate(image.media_type, image.data_base64)
            except ImageValidationError:
                offending.append("images")
                break

    return offending


def submit_review(
    product_id: str,
    author_identity: str,
    rating: object,
    text: object,
    title: object = None,
    images: list[ReviewImageInput] | None = None,
    *,
    store: ReviewStore | None = None,
    images_store: ImageStore | None = None,
) -> Review:
    """Validate and create a ``pending`` review for a product.

    Args:
        product_id: The product being reviewed (must exist in the catalog).
        author_identity: The authoring account's non-sensitive identity.
        rating: Submitted integer rating.
        text: Submitted review body.
        title: Optional submitted title.
        images: Submitted image inputs (0..3).
        store: Review store to use; defaults to the shared in-process store.
        images_store: Image store to use; defaults to the shared local store.

    Returns:
        The created ``Review`` with ``moderation_state == "pending"``.

    Raises:
        ProductNotFoundError: If the product does not exist.
        DuplicateReviewError: If the author already reviewed this product.
        ReviewValidationError: If any field violates its rule; the error names
            the exact offending fields and contains no credential values.
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    active_images = images_store if images_store is not None else image_store
    submitted_images = images if images is not None else []

    # The product must exist so the review associates with a real catalog item.
    if catalog.get_product(product_id) is None:
        raise ProductNotFoundError(product_id)

    offending = _validate_submission_fields(rating, text, title, submitted_images)
    if offending:
        raise ReviewValidationError(
            offending_fields=offending,
            message=(
                "The review could not be submitted. Please correct the "
                "following field(s): " + ", ".join(offending) + "."
            ),
        )

    # One review per author per product (Assumption A1).
    if active_store.find_by_author_and_product(author_identity, product_id) is not None:
        raise DuplicateReviewError()

    # All fields valid: store images (validated again inside the store) and
    # build the pending review. Narrow types now that validation has passed.
    assert isinstance(rating, int)
    assert isinstance(text, str)
    stored_images: list[ReviewImage] = []
    for image in submitted_images:
        image_id, filename = active_images.store(image.media_type, image.data_base64)
        stored_images.append(
            ReviewImage(id=image_id, media_type=image.media_type, filename=filename)
        )

    review = Review(
        id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        product_id=product_id,
        author_identity=author_identity,
        rating=rating,
        title=title if isinstance(title, str) and title != "" else None,
        text=text,
        images=stored_images,
        moderation_state="pending",
    )
    return active_store.add(review)


def list_pending_reviews(*, store: ReviewStore | None = None) -> list[Review]:
    """Return the Moderation_Queue: all reviews in ``pending`` (R3.1, R3.5)."""
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    return active_store.list_by_state("pending")


def approve_review(review_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None) -> Review:
    """Approve a pending review, a terminal transition (R3.3, R3.7)."""
    return _decide_review(review_id, "approved", store=store)


def reject_review(review_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None) -> Review:
    """Reject a pending review, a terminal transition (R3.4, R3.7)."""
    return _decide_review(review_id, "rejected", store=store)


def _decide_review(
    review_id: str,
    new_state: str,
    *,
    store: ReviewStore | None = None,
) -> Review:
    """Apply a terminal moderation decision to a pending review.

    Raises:
        ModerationError: If the review is unknown, or if it is not ``pending``
            (a decided review cannot be moved again; Assumption A4).
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store

    review = active_store.get(review_id)
    if review is None:
        raise ModerationError(
            code="review_not_found",
            message="The review to moderate does not exist.",
        )
    if review.moderation_state != "pending":
        raise ModerationError(
            code="already_decided",
            message="This review has already been moderated and cannot be changed.",
        )

    updated = review.model_copy(update={"moderation_state": new_state})
    stored = active_store.replace(updated)

    # Stage 3 (Requirement 5.5): a moderation decision changes public review
    # visibility. The review-listing endpoint is intentionally uncached, so an
    # approval is already immediately visible; we additionally invalidate the
    # shared response cache here so freshness is enforced from a single,
    # obvious point even if review responses were cached in a future
    # extension. The import is local to avoid any import cycle at module load.
    from app.services import response_cache

    response_cache.invalidate()
    return stored


def list_approved_reviews(
    product_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None
) -> list[Review]:
    """Return the Visible_Reviews (approved) for a product (R4.1, R4.2)."""
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    return [
        review
        for review in active_store.list_by_product(product_id)
        if review.moderation_state == "approved"
    ]


def rating_summary(
    product_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None
) -> RatingSummary:
    """Return the rating summary from approved reviews only (R4.3, R4.5).

    The count is the number of approved reviews; the average is the mean of
    their ratings (0 when there are none). The average is rounded to two
    decimal places for a stable display value.
    """
    approved = list_approved_reviews(product_id, store=store)
    count = len(approved)
    if count == 0:
        return RatingSummary(count=0, average=0.0)
    average = sum(review.rating for review in approved) / count
    return RatingSummary(count=count, average=round(average, 2))


def own_review(
    product_id: str,
    author_identity: str,
    *,
    store: ReviewStore | None = None,
) -> Review | None:
    """Return the author's own review for a product if it is not approved.

    Supports showing an author the state of their own non-approved submission
    (Requirement 4.6). An already-approved own review appears in the public
    list, so it is not returned here to avoid duplication.
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    review = active_store.find_by_author_and_product(author_identity, product_id)
    if review is None or review.moderation_state == "approved":
        return None
    return review

</file>

    """Validate and create a ``pending`` review for a product.

    Args:
        product_id: The product being reviewed (must exist in the catalog).
        author_identity: The authoring account's non-sensitive identity.
        rating: Submitted integer rating.
        text: Submitted review body.
        title: Optional submitted title.
        images: Submitted image inputs (0..3).
        store: Review store to use; defaults to the shared in-process store.
        images_store: Image store to use; defaults to the shared local store.

    Returns:
        The created ``Review`` with ``moderation_state == "pending"``.

    Raises:
        ProductNotFoundError: If the product does not exist.
        DuplicateReviewError: If the author already reviewed this product.
        ReviewValidationError: If any field violates its rule; the error names
            the exact offending fields and contains no credential values.
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    active_images = images_store if images_store is not None else image_store
    submitted_images = images if images is not None else []

    # The product must exist so the review associates with a real catalog item.
    if catalog.get_product(product_id) is None:
        raise ProductNotFoundError(product_id)

    offending = _validate_submission_fields(rating, text, title, submitted_images)
    if offending:
        raise ReviewValidationError(
            offending_fields=offending,
            message=(
                "The review could not be submitted. Please correct the "
                "following field(s): " + ", ".join(offending) + "."
            ),
        )

    # One review per author per product (Assumption A1).
    if active_store.find_by_author_and_product(author_identity, product_id) is not None:
        raise DuplicateReviewError()

    # All fields valid: store images (validated again inside the store) and
    # build the pending review. Narrow types now that validation has passed.
    assert isinstance(rating, int)
    assert isinstance(text, str)
    stored_images: list[ReviewImage] = []
    for image in submitted_images:
        image_id, filename = active_images.store(image.media_type, image.data_base64)
        stored_images.append(
            ReviewImage(id=image_id, media_type=image.media_type, filename=filename)
        )

    review = Review(
        id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        product_id=product_id,
        author_identity=author_identity,
        rating=rating,
        title=title if isinstance(title, str) and title != "" else None,
        text=text,
        images=stored_images,
        moderation_state="pending",
    )
    return active_store.add(review)


def list_pending_reviews(*, store: ReviewStore | None = None) -> list[Review]:
    """Return the Moderation_Queue: all reviews in ``pending`` (R3.1, R3.5)."""
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    return active_store.list_by_state("pending")


def approve_review(review_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None) -> Review:
    """Approve a pending review, a terminal transition (R3.3, R3.7)."""
    return _decide_review(review_id, "approved", store=store)


def reject_review(review_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None) -> Review:
    """Reject a pending review, a terminal transition (R3.4, R3.7)."""
    return _decide_review(review_id, "rejected", store=store)


def _decide_review(
    review_id: str,
    new_state: str,
    *,
    store: ReviewStore | None = None,
) -> Review:
    """Apply a terminal moderation decision to a pending review.

    Raises:
        ModerationError: If the review is unknown, or if it is not ``pending``
            (a decided review cannot be moved again; Assumption A4).
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store

    review = active_store.get(review_id)
    if review is None:
        raise ModerationError(
            code="review_not_found",
            message="The review to moderate does not exist.",
        )
    if review.moderation_state != "pending":
        raise ModerationError(
            code="already_decided",
            message="This review has already been moderated and cannot be changed.",
        )

    updated = review.model_copy(update={"moderation_state": new_state})
    stored = active_store.replace(updated)

    # Stage 3 (Requirement 5.5): a moderation decision changes public review
    # visibility. The review-listing endpoint is intentionally uncached, so an
    # approval is already immediately visible; we additionally invalidate the
    # shared response cache here so freshness is enforced from a single,
    # obvious point even if review responses were cached in a future
    # extension. The import is local to avoid any import cycle at module load.
    from app.services import response_cache

    response_cache.invalidate()
    return stored


def list_approved_reviews(
    product_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None
) -> list[Review]:
    """Return the Visible_Reviews (approved) for a product (R4.1, R4.2)."""
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    return [
        review
        for review in active_store.list_by_product(product_id)
        if review.moderation_state == "approved"
    ]


def rating_summary(
    product_id: str, *, store: ReviewStore | None = None
) -> RatingSummary:
    """Return the rating summary from approved reviews only (R4.3, R4.5).

    The count is the number of approved reviews; the average is the mean of
    their ratings (0 when there are none). The average is rounded to two
    decimal places for a stable display value.
    """
    approved = list_approved_reviews(product_id, store=store)
    count = len(approved)
    if count == 0:
        return RatingSummary(count=0, average=0.0)
    average = sum(review.rating for review in approved) / count
    return RatingSummary(count=count, average=round(average, 2))


def own_review(
    product_id: str,
    author_identity: str,
    *,
    store: ReviewStore | None = None,
) -> Review | None:
    """Return the author's own review for a product if it is not approved.

    Supports showing an author the state of their own non-approved submission
    (Requirement 4.6). An already-approved own review appears in the public
    list, so it is not returned here to avoid duplication.
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else review_store
    review = active_store.find_by_author_and_product(author_identity, product_id)
    if review is None or review.moderation_state == "approved":
        return None
    return review

"""Sign-in / sign-out service (authentication business logic).

This service validates sign-in input, verifies the submitted credential
against the stored ``passwordHash``, and establishes or ends an in-process
``Session`` for the running service. It implements:

- Sign-in that accepts an ``identifier`` and ``password``, establishes an
  active ``Session`` on complete, valid input (Requirements 6.1, 6.9), and
  raises a uniform authentication failure on incomplete/invalid input without
  exposing internal detail, hashes, or submitted credential values
  (Requirements 6.3, 7.4).
- Sign-out that ends the active ``Session`` (Requirement 6.6).

The ``password`` is accepted only as transient input; it is never stored on
the session and never returned (Requirements 7.2, 7.3). The session itself
holds only ``active`` and ``customerId`` (no credential value).

Session state is kept as simple module-level state representing the single
active session of the running demonstration service, consistent with the
``Session`` model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from app.data.accounts import AccountStore, account_store
from app.models.session import Session
from app.services.password_verify import verify_password


class AuthenticationError(Exception):
    """Raised when sign-in input is incomplete or invalid.

    The message indicates the authentication failure without revealing
    internal system details, password hashes, or submitted credential values
    (Requirements 6.3, 7.4).
    """


# A single, generic failure message. It is deliberately uniform for every
# incomplete or invalid sign-in so the response never reveals whether the
# identifier exists or why verification failed (Requirements 6.3, 7.4).
AUTH_FAILURE_MESSAGE = "Sign-in failed: the provided sign-in information is incomplete or invalid."


# Module-level representation of the running service's single active session.
# Starts inactive (no Session). This mirrors the Session model's shape.
_current_session: Session = Session(active=False, customer_id=None)


def _is_blank(value: object) -> bool:
    """Return whether a credential input is missing or effectively empty."""
    return not isinstance(value, str) or value.strip() == ""


def sign_in(
    identifier: str,
    password: str,
    *,
    store: AccountStore | None = None,
) -> Session:
    """Validate credentials and establish an active ``Session``.

    Args:
        identifier: The submitted credential identifier.
        password: The submitted plain-text credential value (transient input;
            never stored or returned).
        store: Account store to look the account up in. Defaults to the shared
            in-process ``account_store``; injectable for tests.

    Returns:
        The active ``Session`` for the identified Customer. The returned
        session carries no password or credential value.

    Raises:
        AuthenticationError: If the input is incomplete (missing identifier or
            password) or invalid (unknown identifier or wrong password). The
            error carries only a uniform failure message.
    """
    account_lookup = store if store is not None else account_store

    # Reject incomplete input before any lookup (Requirement 6.3).
    if _is_blank(identifier) or _is_blank(password):
        raise AuthenticationError(AUTH_FAILURE_MESSAGE)

    account = account_lookup.get_by_identifier(identifier)

    # Unknown identifier or non-matching password both yield the same uniform
    # failure, so the response never distinguishes the two cases (R6.3, R7.4).
    if account is None or not verify_password(password, account.password_hash):
        raise AuthenticationError(AUTH_FAILURE_MESSAGE)

    global _current_session
    # Stage 2 (Assumption A5): the session records whether the authenticated
    # account is a moderator so the moderation endpoints can guard on it. This
    # is additive; a regular customer account yields is_moderator=False, which
    # is the Stage 1 behavior.
    _current_session = Session(
        active=True,
        customer_id=account.id,
        is_moderator=account.is_moderator,
    )
    # Return a copy so callers cannot mutate the stored session state.
    return _current_session.model_copy()


def sign_out() -> Session:
    """End the active ``Session``, returning the resulting inactive session.

    Signing out always results in a state in which no Session is active
    (Requirement 6.6), whether or not a Session was active beforehand.
    """
    global _current_session
    _current_session = Session(active=False, customer_id=None)
    return _current_session.model_copy()


def get_current_session() -> Session:
    """Return a copy of the current in-process session state."""
    return _current_session.model_copy()


def reset_session() -> None:
    """Reset session state to inactive. Provided so tests start from a known state."""
    global _current_session
    _current_session = Session(active=False, customer_id=None)

<content>
"""Registration service (service layer).

Implements account registration for the credential contract: an ``identifier``
and a ``password`` (Requirement 5.1). The service validates that every required
item is present and conforms to its expected format; on success it creates a
``Customer`` account, storing the password only as ``passwordHash`` and never
returning it (Requirements 5.6, 7.3).

On failure it raises a structured error that names the exact set of offending
items — each empty required item (Requirement 5.3) and each non-conforming item
(Requirement 5.4) — and that never echoes the submitted credential values
(Requirement 5.5). An already-taken identifier is reported as a conflict
without exposing internal detail.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from app.data.accounts import AccountStore, account_store
from app.models.customer import Customer

# The required items of the credential contract. The contract is intentionally
# the minimum (identifier + password); no additional fields are invented
# (Requirement 5.1 and the design's Customer model).
REQUIRED_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("identifier", "password")


@dataclass
class RegistrationError(Exception):
    """Structured registration failure that identifies offending items.

    The error carries machine-usable sets of offending field names so the API
    layer can build a safe JSON error. It never carries any submitted
    credential value, so error output cannot echo credentials (Requirement
    5.5).

    Attributes:
        empty_fields: Required items that were missing or empty (R5.3).
        non_conforming_fields: Items present but not conforming to their
            expected format (R5.4).
        message: A short, safe summary that contains no credential values.
    """

    empty_fields: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    non_conforming_fields: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    message: str = "Registration input is invalid."

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - trivial
        return self.message


@dataclass
class IdentifierTakenError(Exception):
    """An account already exists for the submitted identifier.

    Reported without echoing the submitted identifier value or any other
    credential value (Requirements 5.5, 7.4).
    """

    message: str = "An account with the provided identifier already exists."

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - trivial
        return self.message


def _is_present_and_conforming(value: object) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    """Classify a single submitted item.

    Returns ``(is_empty, is_non_conforming)``:
        - ``is_empty`` is True when the item is missing or, after trimming
          surrounding whitespace, has no characters (Requirement 5.3).
        - ``is_non_conforming`` is True when the item is present and non-empty
          but does not conform to its expected format: for this credential
          contract the expected format is a text value, so a non-string
          present value is non-conforming (Requirement 5.4).

    An item is never reported as both empty and non-conforming.
    """
    if value is None:
        return True, False
    if isinstance(value, str):
        # Empty or whitespace-only text is treated as an empty required item.
        if value.strip() == "":
            return True, False
        # A non-empty text value conforms to the expected text format.
        return False, False
    # Present but not text: it does not conform to the expected format.
    return False, True


def register(
    identifier: object,
    password: object,
    store: AccountStore | None = None,
) -> Customer:
    """Register a new ``Customer`` account from registration input.

    Args:
        identifier: The submitted credential identifier.
        password: The submitted plain-text password (used only to compute the
            stored hash; never retained or returned).
        store: Account store to use; defaults to the shared in-process store.

    Returns:
        The created ``Customer``. Its ``password_hash`` is a one-way hash, and
        no readable plain-text password is present on it (Requirement 7.3).

    Raises:
        RegistrationError: If any required item is empty or any item does not
            conform to its expected format. The error names the exact offending
            items and contains no submitted credential values (R5.3, R5.4,
            R5.5).
        IdentifierTakenError: If an account already exists for the identifier.
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else account_store

    submitted: dict[str, object] = {
        "identifier": identifier,
        "password": password,
    }

    empty_fields: list[str] = []
    non_conforming_fields: list[str] = []
    for name in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
        is_empty, is_non_conforming = _is_present_and_conforming(submitted[name])
        if is_empty:
            empty_fields.append(name)
        elif is_non_conforming:
            non_conforming_fields.append(name)

    if empty_fields or non_conforming_fields:
        # Build a safe message that lists only field names, never values.
        parts: list[str] = []
        if empty_fields:
            parts.append(
                "Required field(s) missing: " + ", ".join(empty_fields)
            )
        if non_conforming_fields:
            parts.append(
                "Field(s) with invalid format: "
                + ", ".join(non_conforming_fields)
            )
        raise RegistrationError(
            empty_fields=empty_fields,
            non_conforming_fields=non_conforming_fields,
            message="; ".join(parts) + ".",
        )

    # Both items are present and conforming: safe to narrow to text.
    assert isinstance(identifier, str)
    assert isinstance(password, str)

    if active_store.has_account(identifier):
        raise IdentifierTakenError()

    # Lazy import keeps the hashing dependency out of the import path for
    # callers (such as validation-only tests) that never create an account.
    from app.services.password import hash_password

    password_hash = hash_password(password)
    return active_store.create_account(identifier, password_hash)

"""Checkout confirmation service (business logic for the simulated purchase).

This service builds the non-persistent confirmation summary for a
Simulated_Purchase from the submitted cart contents and the shared catalog
data (Requirements 10.1, 10.2). It resolves each submitted product's name and
unit price from catalog data by ``productId`` so product information stays
consistent across the journey (R11), computes ``lineTotal = unitPrice *
quantity`` and ``total = sum(lineTotal)``, and marks the confirmation as
simulated.

Nothing is persisted: no order record is stored and the confirmation carries
no order ID and no creation timestamp (R10.1). The empty-cart guard (R9.5),
enforced on the frontend before the call, is re-checked here by rejecting an
empty submission.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from app.data import catalog
from app.models.checkout import (
    CheckoutConfirmation,
    CheckoutConfirmationItem,
    CheckoutRequest,
)


class CheckoutError(Exception):
    """Raised when a checkout submission cannot be confirmed.

    Carries a stable machine-readable ``code`` and a human-readable
    ``message`` so the API layer can return a structured JSON error without
    leaking internal detail (Error Handling section of the design).

    Attributes:
        code: Stable error code identifying the failure category.
        message: Human-readable description of the failure.
    """

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.message = message


def confirm_checkout(request: CheckoutRequest) -> CheckoutConfirmation:
    """Build the non-persistent confirmation summary for a Simulated_Purchase.

    Resolves each submitted item's product details (name, unit price) from the
    shared catalog data by ``productId``, computes line totals and the overall
    total, and returns a confirmation marked as simulated. No order record is
    stored and no order ID or creation timestamp is produced (R10.1, R10.2).

    Args:
        request: The submitted cart contents (product identifiers and
            quantities).

    Returns:
        The confirmation summary with per-item lines, the summed total, and
        ``simulated=True``.

    Raises:
        CheckoutError: If the submission is empty (server-side empty-cart
            guard, R9.5), if any quantity is not positive, or if a submitted
            ``productId`` does not resolve to a catalog product.
    """
    # Server-side re-check of the empty-cart guard (R9.5): an empty submission
    # must not be treated as a valid purchase.
    if not request.items:
        raise CheckoutError(
            code="empty_cart",
            message="Cannot confirm a simulated purchase with an empty cart.",
        )

    summary_items: list[CheckoutConfirmationItem] = []
    for item in request.items:
        if item.quantity <= 0:
            raise CheckoutError(
                code="invalid_quantity",
                message=(
                    "Each submitted item must have a quantity of at least one."
                ),
            )

        product = catalog.get_product(item.product_id)
        if product is None:
            # The submitted cart references a product that is not in the shared
            # catalog data, so a consistent summary cannot be built (R11).
            raise CheckoutError(
                code="unknown_product",
                message="A submitted item does not match a known product.",
            )

        line_total = product.price * item.quantity
        summary_items.append(
            CheckoutConfirmationItem(
                product_id=product.id,
                name=product.name,
                unit_price=product.price,
                quantity=item.quantity,
                line_total=line_total,
            )
        )

    total = sum(line.line_total for line in summary_items)

    return CheckoutConfirmation(items=summary_items, total=total, simulated=True)

"""Catalog retrieval service (service layer).

This service exposes the catalog business operations the API layer depends on.
It returns the shared demonstration product data read from the data-access
layer, keeping product identity, name, and price consistent across the whole
journey (Requirements 1.1, 1.3, 1.5, 11.1). It contains no HTTP concerns: the
API layer maps the results to responses and status codes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from app.data import catalog as catalog_data
from app.models.product import Product


class ProductNotFoundError(Exception):
    """Raised when a requested product id does not exist in the catalog.

    The API layer catches this and maps it to a structured 404 JSON response
    (Requirements 1.4). The offending id is carried so the message can name it
    without exposing internal detail or stack traces.
    """

    def __init__(self, product_id: str) -> None:
        self.product_id = product_id
        super().__init__(f"Product not found: {product_id}")


def list_products() -> list[Product]:
    """Return all catalog products as the shared demonstration data.

    This is the single source used across catalog, cart, and checkout so the
    product identity, name, and price stay consistent (Requirements 1.5, 11.1).
    """
    return catalog_data.list_products()


def get_product(product_id: str) -> Product:
    """Return the product with the given id.

    Args:
        product_id: The stable product identity to resolve.

    Returns:
        The matching :class:`Product`.

    Raises:
        ProductNotFoundError: If no product has the given id.
    """
    product = catalog_data.get_product(product_id)
    if product is None:
        raise ProductNotFoundError(product_id)
    return product

"""Bounded, TTL-expiring in-process response cache (service layer, Stage 3).

This module provides a small, self-contained cache used by the catalog cache
middleware to avoid recomputing the session-independent public catalog reads
(``GET /products`` and ``GET /products/{id}``). It is deliberately minimal and
local: no external cache server, no persistence, no paid service.

Safety properties (Stage 3 Requirements 5.2, 5.3, 5.5; Assumptions A3, A4):

- **Bounded size.** The cache holds at most ``max_entries`` entries. When full,
  the oldest-inserted entry is evicted (insertion-ordered eviction), so memory
  is bounded regardless of traffic.
- **Bounded staleness.** Each entry carries an absolute expiry timestamp; a
  ``get`` past expiry is a miss and the stale entry is dropped. No entry can be
  served indefinitely.
- **User-independence.** Only session-independent responses are ever stored (the
  middleware enforces this), so a single shared entry is correct for every
  caller and cannot leak one user's data to another.
- **Explicit invalidation.** ``invalidate`` clears entries (optionally by
  predicate) so a state change elsewhere (e.g. a moderation decision) can force
  freshness even though the catalog itself is unaffected by that change.

The cache is guarded by a ``threading.Lock`` so it is safe under the default
Uvicorn worker. Configuration comes from the environment with safe defaults.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import threading
import time
from collections import OrderedDict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable


def _env_int(name: str, default: int) -> int:
    """Read a non-negative integer env var, falling back to ``default``."""
    raw = os.environ.get(name)
    if raw is None:
        return default
    try:
        value = int(raw)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default
    return value if value >= 0 else default


# Configuration (Assumption A4). TTL of 0 disables caching entirely; the
# middleware then behaves as a pass-through that still marks sensitive routes
# ``no-store``.
DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS = _env_int("CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS", 30)
DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES = _env_int("CATALOG_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES", 256)


@dataclass
class CacheEntry:
    """A stored response body with its media type and absolute expiry time."""

    body: bytes
    media_type: str
    expires_at: float


class BoundedTTLCache:
    """An in-process cache bounded by entry count and per-entry TTL."""

    def __init__(self, *, ttl_seconds: int, max_entries: int) -> None:
        self._ttl_seconds = max(0, ttl_seconds)
        self._max_entries = max(1, max_entries)
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._entries: "OrderedDict[str, CacheEntry]" = OrderedDict()

    @property
    def ttl_seconds(self) -> int:
        """The per-entry time-to-live in seconds (0 means caching disabled)."""
        return self._ttl_seconds

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether caching is active (a positive TTL)."""
        return self._ttl_seconds > 0

    def get(self, key: str) -> CacheEntry | None:
        """Return a live entry for ``key`` or ``None`` (miss or expired)."""
        if not self.enabled:
            return None
        now = time.monotonic()
        with self._lock:
            entry = self._entries.get(key)
            if entry is None:
                return None
            if entry.expires_at <= now:
                # Expired: drop it and report a miss so it is never reused.
                del self._entries[key]
                return None
            # Mark as recently used for insertion-ordered freshness.
            self._entries.move_to_end(key)
            return entry

    def set(self, key: str, body: bytes, media_type: str) -> None:
        """Store a response body for ``key`` with the configured TTL."""
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        expires_at = time.monotonic() + self._ttl_seconds
        with self._lock:
            self._entries[key] = CacheEntry(
                body=body, media_type=media_type, expires_at=expires_at
            )
            self._entries.move_to_end(key)
            # Evict oldest entries until within the bound.
            while len(self._entries) > self._max_entries:
                self._entries.popitem(last=False)

    def invalidate(self, predicate: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None) -> int:
        """Drop all entries, or only those whose key matches ``predicate``.

        Returns the number of entries removed. Called on moderation state
        changes so freshness is enforced even if review responses were cached
        in a future extension (Requirement 5.5).
        """
        with self._lock:
            if predicate is None:
                removed = len(self._entries)
                self._entries.clear()
                return removed
            keys = [key for key in self._entries if predicate(key)]
            for key in keys:
                del self._entries[key]
            return len(keys)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove all entries. Provided so tests start from a known state."""
        with self._lock:
            self._entries.clear()


# Module-level singleton used by the middleware and the invalidation hook.
response_cache = BoundedTTLCache(
    ttl_seconds=DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS,
    max_entries=DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES,
)


def invalidate() -> int:
    """Invalidate the whole shared cache (moderation-change hook, R5.5)."""
    return response_cache.invalidate()

"""Shared password hashing helper (service layer).

Authentication accepts a password only as request input. It is never kept or
returned as readable plain text; it is stored solely as a one-way hash
(Requirements 7.2, 7.3). This module centralizes the hashing/verification so
registration and sign-in share one consistent credential-handling policy.

The hashing uses the established ``bcrypt`` library, a standard one-way
password hashing scheme appropriate for the demonstration scope. No raw
password value is logged, stored, or returned by anything here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bcrypt

# bcrypt operates on a 72-byte secret limit. Longer inputs are reduced to a
# fixed-size digest first so any length of password can be hashed consistently,
# while the stored value remains a one-way hash and never the plain text.
import hashlib


def _to_secret(password: str) -> bytes:
    """Return the bytes bcrypt should hash for the given password.

    bcrypt silently truncates anything beyond 72 bytes, so passwords longer
    than that are pre-hashed to a fixed-length digest. This keeps the full
    password material contributing to the stored hash without ever retaining
    the readable plain text.
    """
    raw = password.encode("utf-8")
    if len(raw) > 72:
        # Pre-hash to a 64-char hex digest (<= 72 bytes) before bcrypt.
        return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest().encode("ascii")
    return raw


def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    """Return a one-way hash of the given plain-text password.

    The returned value is a bcrypt hash, never the readable plain-text
    password, so it is safe to store as ``passwordHash`` (Requirement 7.3). The
    plain-text ``password`` argument is only read to compute the hash and is
    not retained.
    """
    hashed = bcrypt.hashpw(_to_secret(password), bcrypt.gensalt())
    return hashed.decode("ascii")


def verify_password(password: str, password_hash: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``password`` matches the stored ``password_hash``.

    Used by sign-in to check a submitted credential against the stored hash
    without ever reconstructing the plain-text password.
    """
    try:
        return bcrypt.checkpw(_to_secret(password), password_hash.encode("ascii"))
    except ValueError:
        # A malformed stored hash never matches.
        return False

<content>
"""Password verification helper (sign-in side).

This module provides a single ``verify_password`` helper used by the sign-in
service to check a submitted plain-text ``password`` against a stored
``passwordHash`` (Requirements 6.9, 7.3). The plain-text password is accepted
only as transient input here; it is never stored or returned, and only the
boolean result of the comparison leaves this module.

Verification uses the ``bcrypt`` library directly so the stored credential is
never readable plain text and so verification works against any standard
bcrypt hash (``$2a$``/``$2b$``/``$2y$``) regardless of which component produced
it. If the registration side introduces a shared ``app.services.password``
module exposing a ``verify_password`` function, this helper transparently
delegates to it so a single scheme is used across registration and sign-in;
otherwise it verifies locally.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bcrypt

# bcrypt only considers the first 72 bytes of a secret. Truncate consistently
# so verification agrees with any hashing side that follows the same rule.
_BCRYPT_MAX_BYTES = 72


def verify_password(password: str, password_hash: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``password`` matches the stored ``password_hash``.

    Args:
        password: The submitted plain-text credential value (transient input;
            never stored or returned).
        password_hash: The stored hashed credential to compare against.

    Returns:

        missing, malformed, or non-string stored hash yields ``False`` rather
        than raising, so sign-in surfaces a uniform authentication failure
        without leaking internal detail (Requirement 7.4).
    """

    # and sign-in agree on a single scheme. Imported lazily to avoid a hard
    # dependency on a module another task may own.
    try:  # pragma: no cover - exercised only once the shared module exists
        from app.services.password import verify_password as shared_verify

        return bool(shared_verify(password, password_hash))
    except Exception:
        pass

    if not isinstance(password, str) or not isinstance(password_hash, str):
        return False
    if not password_hash:
        return False

    secret = password.encode("utf-8")[:_BCRYPT_MAX_BYTES]
    try:
        return bcrypt.checkpw(secret, password_hash.encode("utf-8"))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        # An unrecognized/corrupt hash must not raise through to the client.
        return False

"""Demonstration moderator seeding (service layer, Stage 2).

The moderation workflow requires a moderator account (Assumption A5). To make
the workflow demonstrable immediately, a single built-in demonstration
moderator is seeded into the shared account store at startup. The credentials
are fixed constants documented in the project README so a reviewer can sign in
as the moderator without any extra setup.

Seeding is idempotent: calling it when the moderator already exists does
nothing. The password is stored only as a one-way hash, reusing the Stage 1
password-hashing policy; the plain-text demo password is a documented
convenience for the local demo and is never stored or returned.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

from app.data.accounts import AccountStore, account_store
from app.models.customer import Customer
from app.services.password import hash_password

# Fixed demonstration moderator credentials. Documented in the README so the
# moderation workflow can be exercised immediately. These are intentionally
# simple because this is a local, non-production demonstration.
MODERATOR_IDENTIFIER = "moderator"
MODERATOR_PASSWORD = "moderator123"


def seed_moderator(store: AccountStore | None = None) -> Customer:
    """Ensure the demonstration moderator account exists.

    Idempotent: if an account already exists for the moderator identifier it is
    returned unchanged; otherwise a new moderator ``Customer`` is created with
    ``is_moderator=True`` and a hashed password.

    Args:
        store: Account store to seed into; defaults to the shared in-process
            ``account_store``.

    Returns:
        The seeded (or pre-existing) moderator ``Customer``.
    """
    active_store = store if store is not None else account_store

    existing = active_store.get_by_identifier(MODERATOR_IDENTIFIER)
    if existing is not None:
        return existing

    # The AccountStore.create_account helper does not set is_moderator, so build
    # the moderator Customer directly and register it through the store's
    # internal mapping via create then rely on a moderator-aware create path.
    moderator = Customer(
        id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        identifier=MODERATOR_IDENTIFIER,
        password_hash=hash_password(MODERATOR_PASSWORD),
        is_moderator=True,
    )
    active_store.add_customer(moderator)
    return moderator.model_copy()

"""In-process account storage (data-access layer).

This module keeps account data in in-process storage for the running service
(Requirement 14.6). It supports reading and writing Customer accounts and
nothing else: it stores no order records, because checkout confirmation is
non-persistent (Requirements 6.9, 7.3, and the non-persistent checkout).

The password is never handled here as plain text. Callers pass an already
hashed credential (``password_hash``); this layer only stores and reads it.
Account identities are generated here so each stored account has a stable id.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

from app.models.customer import Customer


class AccountStore:
    """In-process read/write store for Customer accounts.

    Accounts are indexed by their credential ``identifier`` so sign-in can look
    an account up by the value the person provides. The store holds no order
    records and no plain-text passwords.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._accounts_by_identifier: dict[str, Customer] = {}

    def has_account(self, identifier: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether an account with the given identifier exists."""
        return identifier in self._accounts_by_identifier

    def get_by_identifier(self, identifier: str) -> Customer | None:
        """Return the account for the given identifier, or ``None``.

        Returns a copy so stored account data cannot be mutated by callers.
        """
        account = self._accounts_by_identifier.get(identifier)
        return account.model_copy() if account is not None else None

    def get_by_id(self, customer_id: str) -> Customer | None:
        """Return the account with the given account id, or ``None``.

        Added additively for Stage 2 so a session's ``customer_id`` can be
        resolved to the account's non-sensitive identifier for review
        authorship. Returns a copy so stored data cannot be mutated.
        """
        for account in self._accounts_by_identifier.values():
            if account.id == customer_id:
                return account.model_copy()
        return None

    def create_account(self, identifier: str, password_hash: str) -> Customer:
        """Create and store a new account, returning the stored Customer.

        Args:
            identifier: The credential identifier for the new account.
            password_hash: The already-hashed credential to store. This layer
                never receives or stores a readable plain-text password.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If an account with this identifier already exists.
        """
        if identifier in self._accounts_by_identifier:
            raise ValueError(f"An account already exists for identifier: {identifier}")

        customer = Customer(
            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            identifier=identifier,
            password_hash=password_hash,
        )
        self._accounts_by_identifier[identifier] = customer
        return customer.model_copy()

    def add_customer(self, customer: Customer) -> Customer:
        """Store a pre-built ``Customer`` account, returning a stored copy.

        Added additively for Stage 2 so a fully-formed account (for example a
        seeded moderator with ``is_moderator=True``) can be stored without the
        ``create_account`` helper's identity generation. Mirrors the copy-on-
        write behavior of the rest of this store.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If an account with this identifier already exists.
        """
        if customer.identifier in self._accounts_by_identifier:
            raise ValueError(
                f"An account already exists for identifier: {customer.identifier}"
            )
        self._accounts_by_identifier[customer.identifier] = customer.model_copy()
        return customer.model_copy()

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove all stored accounts.

        Provided so tests can start from a known-empty in-process store.
        """
        self._accounts_by_identifier.clear()


# Shared in-process account store for the running service. Account data lives
# only for the lifetime of the process; nothing is persisted durably.
account_store = AccountStore()

</content>
</file>

"""In-process review storage (data-access layer, Stage 2).

This module keeps review records in in-process storage for the running service,
mirroring the Stage 1 ``AccountStore`` style: an in-memory dict that returns
copies so callers cannot mutate stored state (Requirement 9.6, Assumption A6).
It stores no credential values and nothing durable; review records live only
for the lifetime of the backend process. Review image bytes are stored
separately on disk by ``review_images.py``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from app.models.review import ModerationState, Review


class ReviewStore:
    """In-process read/write store for reviews.

    Reviews are indexed by their ``id``. All reads return copies so the stored
    data stays immutable to callers. State transitions are performed by
    replacing the stored review with an updated copy.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._reviews_by_id: dict[str, Review] = {}

    def add(self, review: Review) -> Review:
        """Store a new review, returning a copy of the stored record.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a review with the same id already exists.
        """
        if review.id in self._reviews_by_id:
            raise ValueError(f"A review already exists with id: {review.id}")
        self._reviews_by_id[review.id] = review.model_copy(deep=True)
        return review.model_copy(deep=True)

    def get(self, review_id: str) -> Review | None:
        """Return the review with the given id, or ``None``."""
        review = self._reviews_by_id.get(review_id)
        return review.model_copy(deep=True) if review is not None else None

    def list_all(self) -> list[Review]:
        """Return copies of all stored reviews."""
        return [review.model_copy(deep=True) for review in self._reviews_by_id.values()]

    def list_by_product(self, product_id: str) -> list[Review]:
        """Return all reviews associated with the given product."""
        return [
            review.model_copy(deep=True)
            for review in self._reviews_by_id.values()
            if review.product_id == product_id
        ]

    def list_by_state(self, state: ModerationState) -> list[Review]:
        """Return all reviews currently in the given moderation state."""
        return [
            review.model_copy(deep=True)
            for review in self._reviews_by_id.values()
            if review.moderation_state == state
        ]

    def find_by_author_and_product(
        self, author_identity: str, product_id: str
    ) -> Review | None:
        """Return the given author's review for the product, or ``None``.

        Supports the one-review-per-author-per-product rule (Assumption A1).
        """
        for review in self._reviews_by_id.values():
            if (
                review.author_identity == author_identity
                and review.product_id == product_id
            ):
                return review.model_copy(deep=True)
        return None

    def replace(self, review: Review) -> Review:
        """Replace an existing review with an updated copy (used for transitions).

        Raises:
            KeyError: If no review with this id exists.
        """
        if review.id not in self._reviews_by_id:
            raise KeyError(f"No review exists with id: {review.id}")
        self._reviews_by_id[review.id] = review.model_copy(deep=True)
        return review.model_copy(deep=True)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove all stored reviews. Provided so tests start from empty."""
        self._reviews_by_id.clear()


# Shared in-process review store for the running service. Review data lives only
# for the lifetime of the process; nothing is persisted durably.
review_store = ReviewStore()

<content>
"""Local on-disk review image storage (data-access layer, Stage 2).

Review image bytes are the single on-disk artifact in Stage 2 (Assumption A3,
A6). This module validates submitted images (media-type allow-list and size
cap), writes accepted bytes to a local, git-ignored demonstration folder, and
reads them back for serving through the image endpoint. No external object
storage, CDN, or paid service is used (Requirement 2.7).

Images arrive base64-encoded with a declared media type. A rejected
attachment is never written to disk (Requirements 2.3, 2.4, 6.3).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import binascii
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

# Allowed image media types (Assumption A3). Anything else is rejected.
ALLOWED_MEDIA_TYPES: dict[str, str] = {
    "image/jpeg": ".jpg",
    "image/png": ".png",
    "image/gif": ".gif",
    "image/webp": ".webp",
}

# Maximum accepted size for a single decoded image: 2 MB (Assumption A3).
MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024

# Local demonstration folder for stored image bytes. Resolved relative to this
# file so it works regardless of the process working directory.
IMAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "review_images"


class ImageValidationError(Exception):
    """Raised when a submitted image fails validation.

    Carries a stable ``code`` and a safe, human-readable ``message`` so the
    service and API layers can surface a structured error without exposing
    internal detail (Requirement 6.1).
    """

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.message = message


class ImageStore:
    """Validates and stores review image bytes in a local folder."""

    def __init__(self, image_dir: Path | None = None) -> None:
        self._image_dir = image_dir if image_dir is not None else IMAGE_DIR
        self._media_types: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._ensure_dir()

    def _ensure_dir(self) -> None:
        self._image_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def validate(self, media_type: str, data_base64: str) -> bytes:
        """Validate a single image and return its decoded bytes.

        Does not write anything; a caller that wants to persist must call
        :meth:`store`. Raises :class:`ImageValidationError` for an unsupported
        media type, undecodable data, or an oversized image (Requirements 2.3,
        2.4, 6.3).
        """
        if media_type not in ALLOWED_MEDIA_TYPES:
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="unsupported_image_type",
                message=(
                    "Unsupported image type. Allowed types are JPEG, PNG, "
                    "GIF, and WebP."
                ),
            )
        try:
            raw = base64.b64decode(data_base64, validate=True)
        except (binascii.Error, ValueError):
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="invalid_image_data",
                message="An attached image could not be read.",
            )
        if len(raw) == 0:
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="invalid_image_data",
                message="An attached image is empty.",
            )
        if len(raw) > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES:
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="image_too_large",
                message="An attached image exceeds the 2 MB size limit.",
            )
        return raw

    def store(self, media_type: str, data_base64: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Validate and persist a single image.

        Returns ``(image_id, filename)``. Only called after validation passes,
        so a rejected attachment is never written (Requirements 2.5, 6.3).
        """
        raw = self.validate(media_type, data_base64)

"""Local on-disk review image storage (data-access layer, Stage 2).

Review image bytes are the single on-disk artifact in Stage 2 (Assumption A3,
A6). This module validates submitted images (media-type allow-list and size
cap), writes accepted bytes to a local, git-ignored demonstration folder, and
reads them back for serving through the image endpoint. No external object
storage, CDN, or paid service is used (Requirement 2.7).

Images arrive base64-encoded with a declared media type. A rejected
attachment is never written to disk (Requirements 2.3, 2.4, 6.3).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import binascii
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

# Allowed image media types (Assumption A3). Anything else is rejected.
ALLOWED_MEDIA_TYPES: dict[str, str] = {
    "image/jpeg": ".jpg",
    "image/png": ".png",
    "image/gif": ".gif",
    "image/webp": ".webp",
}

# Maximum accepted size for a single decoded image: 2 MB (Assumption A3).
MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024

# Local demonstration folder for stored image bytes. Resolved relative to this
# file so it works regardless of the process working directory.
IMAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "review_images"


class ImageValidationError(Exception):
    """Raised when a submitted image fails validation.

    Carries a stable ``code`` and a safe, human-readable ``message`` so the
    service and API layers can surface a structured error without exposing
    internal detail (Requirement 6.1).
    """

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.message = message


class ImageStore:
    """Validates and stores review image bytes in a local folder."""

    def __init__(self, image_dir: Path | None = None) -> None:
        self._image_dir = image_dir if image_dir is not None else IMAGE_DIR
        self._media_types: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._ensure_dir()

    def _ensure_dir(self) -> None:
        self._image_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def validate(self, media_type: str, data_base64: str) -> bytes:
        """Validate a single image and return its decoded bytes.

        Does not write anything; a caller that wants to persist must call
        :meth:`store`. Raises :class:`ImageValidationError` for an unsupported
        media type, undecodable data, or an oversized image (Requirements 2.3,
        2.4, 6.3).
        """
        if media_type not in ALLOWED_MEDIA_TYPES:
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="unsupported_image_type",
                message=(
                    "Unsupported image type. Allowed types are JPEG, PNG, "
                    "GIF, and WebP."
                ),
            )
        try:
            raw = base64.b64decode(data_base64, validate=True)
        except (binascii.Error, ValueError):
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="invalid_image_data",
                message="An attached image could not be read.",
            )
        if len(raw) == 0:
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="invalid_image_data",
                message="An attached image is empty.",
            )
        if len(raw) > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES:
            raise ImageValidationError(
                code="image_too_large",
                message="An attached image exceeds the 2 MB size limit.",
            )
        return raw

    def store(self, media_type: str, data_base64: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Validate and persist a single image.

        Returns ``(image_id, filename)``. Only called after validation passes,
        so a rejected attachment is never written (Requirements 2.5, 6.3).
        """
        raw = self.validate(media_type, data_base64)
        image_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        extension = ALLOWED_MEDIA_TYPES[media_type]
        filename = f"{image_id}{extension}"
        self._ensure_dir()
        (self._image_dir / filename).write_bytes(raw)
        self._media_types[image_id] = media_type
        return image_id, filename

    def read(self, image_id: str, filename: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
        """Return ``(bytes, media_type)`` for a stored image.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: If the image is not present on disk.
        """
        path = self._image_dir / filename
        if not path.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(image_id)
        media_type = self._media_types.get(image_id)
        if media_type is None:
            # Recover the media type from the extension if the in-memory map
            # was reset (for example after a process restart in the demo).
            media_type = _media_type_from_filename(filename)
        return path.read_bytes(), media_type

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove all stored image files and metadata. Provided for tests."""
        if self._image_dir.exists():
            for child in self._image_dir.iterdir():
                if child.is_file() and child.name != ".gitignore":
                    child.unlink()
        self._media_types.clear()


def _media_type_from_filename(filename: str) -> str:
    """Best-effort media type from a stored filename's extension."""
    suffix = Path(filename).suffix.lower()
    for media_type, extension in ALLOWED_MEDIA_TYPES.items():
        if extension == suffix:
            return media_type
    return "application/octet-stream"


# Shared local image store for the running service.
image_store = ImageStore()

)

    Returns a copy so the shared catalog data stays immutable to callers.

    for product in _CATALOG:

    return None

"""Checkout data models (non-persistent request/response for the simulated purchase).

These models describe the HTTP/JSON contract for ``POST /checkout/confirm``
(Requirement 10). A ``CheckoutRequest`` carries only the submitted cart
contents (product identifiers and quantities); the backend resolves product
details (name, unit price) from the shared catalog data so product information
stays consistent across the journey (Requirements 10.2, 11). The
``CheckoutConfirmation`` is the summary returned for a completed
Simulated_Purchase: it is built from the submitted cart and catalog data, is
never stored, and carries no order identity and no creation timestamp
(Requirements 10.1, 10.2).

Field names are serialized in camelCase (for example ``productId``,
``unitPrice``, ``lineTotal``) to match the HTTP/JSON interface, while Python
identifiers remain snake_case.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel


class _CamelModel(BaseModel):
    """Base model serializing fields in camelCase for the HTTP/JSON interface."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        alias_generator=to_camel,
        populate_by_name=True,
    )


class CheckoutRequestItem(_CamelModel):
    """A single submitted cart line: a product identity and its quantity.

    Attributes:
        product_id: References ``Product.id`` (shared identity, R11).
        quantity: Count of this product in the submitted cart.
    """

    product_id: str
    quantity: int


class CheckoutRequest(_CamelModel):
    """The cart contents submitted for a Simulated_Purchase (R10).

    Carries only product identifiers and quantities; the backend resolves
    product details from catalog data.

    Attributes:
        items: The submitted cart contents.
    """

    items: list[CheckoutRequestItem]


class CheckoutConfirmationItem(_CamelModel):
    """A purchased-items summary line, resolved from the catalog (R10.2, R11).

    Attributes:
        product_id: Stable product identity (shared across the journey).
        name: Product name resolved from catalog data.
        unit_price: Unit price resolved from catalog data.
        quantity: Count of this product in the purchase.
        line_total: ``unit_price * quantity``.
    """

    product_id: str
    name: str
    unit_price: float
    quantity: int
    line_total: float


class CheckoutConfirmation(_CamelModel):
    """The confirmation summary returned for a completed Simulated_Purchase.

    Built from the submitted cart and catalog data and not stored. It carries
    no order identity and no creation timestamp (R10.1, R10.2).

    Attributes:
        items: The purchased-items summary.
        total: Purchased total, equal to the sum of ``line_total`` across items
            (consistent with the cart, R11.5).
        simulated: Always ``True`` — the purchase is fictitious (R10.1).
    """

    items: list[CheckoutConfirmationItem]
    total: float
    simulated: Literal[True] = True

        unit_price: Unit price resolved from catalog data.
        quantity: Count of this product in the purchase.
        line_total: ``unit_price * quantity``.
    """

    product_id: str
    name: str
    unit_price: float
    quantity: int
    line_total: float


class CheckoutConfirmation(_CamelModel):
    """The confirmation summary returned for a completed Simulated_Purchase.

    Built from the submitted cart and catalog data and not stored. It carries
    no order identity and no creation timestamp (R10.1, R10.2).

    Attributes:
        items: The purchased-items summary.
        total: Purchased total, equal to the sum of ``line_total`` across items
            (consistent with the cart, R11.5).
        simulated: Always ``True`` — the purchase is fictitious (R10.1).
    """

    items: list[CheckoutConfirmationItem]
    total: float
    simulated: Literal[True] = True

</content>
